tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

>>> FOR THE CLEAN SESSION ONLY. First, check that .claude/small-beeps-role in this folder says "clean". If it says anything else, stop at once, read nothing further, and tell the owner this message went to the wrong session. <<<

You are the firmware-side (clean) session. The owner may not be watching; take the most reasonable reading, say which you took, and keep going. Setup notes as before (clean folder, privacy rule, no hardware facts here, PRs to main, cumulative, one merge order, questions at the top, stop below 2 GB free). A spec session may work at the same time; never open its branches.

## 0. Start
The owner merged everything through #168 and spec's #155 to #162. Clean setup checks, archive clean-1027's transcript and run tools/check-transcripts.py (review entries as needed), EXPOSURE entry, save this prompt unedited as docs/prompts/clean-1028.md.

## 1. Pin fwtest 0.9.0
#162's merge published fwtest 0.9.0 (a store into its own base register keeps the old value, SR-10). Open the pin PR, run the firmware suite, store tests and ARP suite on it, and report any change. First in your merge order.

## 2. Two more requests from a firmware built on small-beeps (don't name or describe it)
- BR-12, a save that survives a power cut (needed soon): a record rewrite is atomic. If the power goes at any moment during a save, the next start finds either the complete old payload or the complete new one, never neither and never a mix. That includes the large records from BR-9. Keep the old copy until the new one is fully written and verified (a second copy, a log, or alternating slots; your choice, with the space cost stated), and say how much the store region must grow for it. Test it with fwtest's power-cut feature at every point of a save (the flash chip's cut injection), for small and large records.
- BR-11, per-folder compiler flags: tools/build.sh options so a downstream build can give its own source folders their own compiler flags (beside --src and --leave-out), with the base's own files still built with the base's flags. Documented in BUILDING-ON-SMALL-BEEPS.md, deterministic, tested.
Each its own PR, with requirements and DESIGN-NOTES entries.

## 3. Note for the hardware phase
Add to PLAN.md's hardware-phase list: USB MIDI (class-compliant device) for firmwares built on small-beeps (BR-10), so MIDI out reaches a computer or iPad on a real unit, which has no MIDI OUT jack. Nothing to build now.

#
# Creates (or sets up) a clean, firmware-side working folder:
#   tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]
# A blob-less clone with a sparse checkout without the spec-side folders

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Updates a clean folder to its remote's main (or REF), the safe way.
#
#   tools/clean-update.sh [--dir DIR] [REF]      (default: this folder, main)
#
# Clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, set
# by config/claude/clean.json), so no command can download a file the clean
# folder leaves out. A checkout of new commits needs lazy fetching for the
# files it does check out, so this script allows it for exactly one
# fast-forward, then re-applies the sparse checkout and checks that no file
# under a spec-side folder (config/spec-side-folders) reached the disk or the
# folder's .git, nor any spec-side file under another branch (the records
# branch keeps spec-side outputs). Stop and tell the owner if it fails.
#
# The fast-forward runs with --no-stat and -q: a merge summary (diffstat)
# counts the lines of every changed file, and with lazy fetching allowed git
# downloads the excluded files' contents to count them.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dir" ]; then ROOT=$(cd "$2" && pwd); shift 2; fi
ref=${1:-main}
role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$role" = clean ] || { echo "clean-update.sh is for clean folders (role here: ${role:-none})" >&2; exit 2; }

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" merge -q --no-stat --ff-only "origin/$ref"
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" > /dev/null

# The spec-side folders, from the one list (since M3).
SPEC_FOLDERS=$(grep -v '^#' "$ROOT/config/spec-side-folders" | cut -f1)
[ -n "$SPEC_FOLDERS" ] || { echo "STOP: no spec-side folders in config/spec-side-folders"; exit 1; }
# Any path with one of them, or a spec-experiments/ folder, in it.
SPEC_RE="(^|/)(spec-experiments|$(printf '%s\n' "$SPEC_FOLDERS" | paste -sd '|' -))/"
fail=0
for p in $SPEC_FOLDERS; do
    [ ! -e "$ROOT/$p" ] || { echo "STOP: $p is on disk"; fail=1; }
---

content.content:
emulator's package path (which the upstream web build and fwtest's
`--package` share, and the F-Emulator app too, HW-93 and HW-94) and the chip's own chain
(HW-92). Written by session spec-a1-fwsc for a packager of our own
(docs/A1-PLAN.md). No stock package was opened for it; what only a stock
file could show is left open (Q-25, Q-26). HW-91 corrects HW-81's
window address. Offsets are in bytes from the start of the structure
named; all multi-byte fields are little-endian.

### HW-87: JieLi's CRC-16 and the header mask
- Fact: Two rules recur in the package:
  - **CRC-16** ("JieLi's CRC-16" below): polynomial `0x1021`, initial
    value 0, bits taken most significant first, no reflection, no final
    XOR (the CRC-16/XMODEM parameters). Check value: the ASCII bytes
    `123456789` give `0x31C3`. A structure's own CRC sits in its first
    two bytes and covers the rest of it, from byte 2 to its end.
  - **The mask** with a 16-bit seed: keep a 16-bit value `k`, starting at
    the seed; XOR each byte, in order, with `k`'s low 8 bits; after each
    byte, shift `k` left by one, keeping 16 bits, and if `k`'s top bit was
    1 before the shift, XOR it with `0x1021`. The mask is its own inverse.
    The first four mask bytes from seed `0xFFFF` are `FF DF 9F 1F`. The
    "header key `0xFFFF`" below is this mask with seed `0xFFFF`.
  M9-PLAN.md called the CRC CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (initial value `0xFFFF`),
  after RE; that is wrong for these structures: the SDK's own packer and
  the emulator's package path start from 0.
- Sources: SDK `cpu/wl82/tools/packufw/source/JLpack.cpp` lines 23-44
  (the CRC: table of `0x1021` multiples, initial 0) and 181, 198 (a
  head's CRC over the head after its first two bytes, stored first); RE
  `docs/io/11-ota-protocol.md`, "The .fwsc logical image" (the header key
  `0xFFFF`) and "Known open items" (`jl_crc16` named CCITT-FALSE); the
  emulator's package path (HW-93: the mask, and CRCs from 0 that pass on
  the stock packages it boots).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK for the CRC; the mask emulator-only, its seed
  RE)
- Needed by: A1

### HW-88: The package file: header blocks, header, entries
- Fact: A package is a header in blocks, then data:
  - **Blocks.** The file's first 960 bytes are 20 blocks of 48 (`0x30`)
    bytes. In each block the first 47 (`0x2F`) bytes are header data and
    the last is a marker. The 20 data parts, in order, make the **logical
    header** (940 bytes). Everything from file offset 960 on is data,
    plain. The **logical image** is the logical header followed by the
    file from offset 960: logical offset `n` is file offset `n + 20` for
    `n` ≥ 940.
  - **Markers.** Block `i`'s marker (file offset `48·i + 47`) is the
    package's identity's character `i` plus `i + 1` (modulo 256) while
    the identity lasts, and `0x7D` after it; the stock FM-1 package's
    identity is its name (`FM-1_0nn`, 8 characters, so blocks 8 to 19
    carry `0x7D`). The emulator reads the identity back from the markers;
    one that starts with `SMK`, `MKE` or `STARRYKEY` (any case) makes it
    boot the SMK-37 keyboard instead of the FM-1, and if the data byte at
    file offset 1007 (where a 21st block's marker would be) is `0x7D` it
    first tries a longer header, then falls back to 20 blocks. So an FM-1
    package's identity is ASCII, at most 19 characters (ending the
    markers with `0x7D`, as stock does), and starts with none of those.
  - **Header.** The logical header's first 64 (`0x40`) bytes are masked
    with the header key (HW-87). Unmasked: bytes 0-1 the header's
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-63; bytes 8-9 the entry count. RE names the
    header's fields, in order, header CRC, list CRC, image size and entry
    count; where the list CRC and the image size sit, and what they
    cover, is not given (Q-25).
  - **Entries.** Entry `k` is the 80 (`0x50`) bytes at logical offset
    `64 + 80·k`, masked on its own with the header key. Unmasked: bytes
    0-1 its type, type 0 being the **flash image**; bytes 8-11 its data's
    logical offset; bytes 12-15 its data's length. Its name, its CRC and
    its other fields are not given (Q-25). The stock package has eight
    entries, the flash image (`flash.bin`), `info.log`, `USR`, the
    loader's configuration (`isd_config.ini`), the update loader

### HW-90: The app area: the chip key and its scrambling
- Fact: The app area starts at the `app_dir_head` head's offset `A`
  (`0x4000` on the FM-1; HW-91 says why it must be). It is scrambled
  with a 16-bit **chip key**:

    HW-89): let `s` be the sum of `b[0]`-`b[15]` modulo 256; if `s` ≥
    `0xE0`, take `s` = `0xAA`; else if `s` ≤ `0x10`, take `s` = `0x55`.

    `b[15 − i]` is less than `s`, else 0. Any key block gives a key; the
    stock package's gives `0x980F`.

    the chunk at offset `r` from `A` (`r` = 0, 32, 64, …) is masked

    chunk may be shorter. The first chunk is the **area head**, a 32-byte
    head (HW-89's layout, not masked again) whose length field (bytes
    8-11) is the length of the scrambled area from `A`, the area head
    included. Bytes past that length are left as they are.

### HW-87: JieLi's CRC-16 and the header mask
- Fact: Two rules recur in the package:
  - **CRC-16** ("JieLi's CRC-16" below): polynomial `0x1021`, initial
    value 0, bits taken most significant first, no reflection, no final
    XOR (the CRC-16/XMODEM parameters). Check value: the ASCII bytes
    `123456789` give `0x31C3`. A structure's own CRC sits in its first
    two bytes and covers the rest of it, from byte 2 to its end.
  - **The mask** with a 16-bit seed: keep a 16-bit value `k`, starting at
    the seed; XOR each byte, in order, with `k`'s low 8 bits; after each
    byte, shift `k` left by one, keeping 16 bits, and if `k`'s top bit was
    1 before the shift, XOR it with `0x1021`. The mask is its own inverse.
    The first four mask bytes from seed `0xFFFF` are `FF DF 9F 1F`. The
    "header key `0xFFFF`" below is this mask with seed `0xFFFF`.
  M9-PLAN.md called the CRC CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (initial value `0xFFFF`),
  after RE; that is wrong for these structures: the SDK's own packer and
  the emulator's package path start from 0.
- Sources: SDK `cpu/wl82/tools/packufw/source/JLpack.cpp` lines 23-44

### HW-88: The package file: header blocks, header, entries
- Fact: A package is a header in blocks, then data:
  - **Blocks.** The file's first 960 bytes are 20 blocks of 48 (`0x30`)
    bytes. In each block the first 47 (`0x2F`) bytes are header data and
    the last is a marker. The 20 data parts, in order, make the **logical
    header** (940 bytes). Everything from file offset 960 on is data,
    plain. The **logical image** is the logical header followed by the
    file from offset 960: logical offset `n` is file offset `n + 20` for
    `n` ≥ 940.
  - **Markers.** Block `i`'s marker (file offset `48·i + 47`) is the
    package's identity's character `i` plus `i + 1` (modulo 256) while
    the identity lasts, and `0x7D` after it; the stock FM-1 package's
    identity is its name (`FM-1_0nn`, 8 characters, so blocks 8 to 19
    carry `0x7D`). The emulator reads the identity back from the markers;
    one that starts with `SMK`, `MKE` or `STARRYKEY` (any case) makes it
    boot the SMK-37 keyboard instead of the FM-1, and if the data byte at
    file offset 1007 (where a 21st block's marker would be) is `0x7D` it
    first tries a longer header, then falls back to 20 blocks. So an FM-1
    package's identity is ASCII, at most 19 characters (ending the
    markers with `0x7D`, as stock does), and starts with none of those.
  - **Header.** The logical header's first 64 (`0x40`) bytes are masked
    with the header key (HW-87). Unmasked: bytes 0-1 the header's
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-63; bytes 8-9 the entry count. RE names the
    header's fields, in order, header CRC, list CRC, image size and entry
    count; where the list CRC and the image size sit, and what they
    cover, is not given (Q-25).
  - **Entries.** Entry `k` is the 80 (`0x50`) bytes at logical offset
    `64 + 80·k`, masked on its own with the header key. Unmasked: bytes
    0-1 its type, type 0 being the **flash image**; bytes 8-11 its data's
    logical offset; bytes 12-15 its data's length. Its name, its CRC and
    its other fields are not given (Q-25). The stock package has eight
    entries, the flash image (`flash.bin`), `info.log`, `USR`, the
    loader's configuration (`isd_config.ini`), the update loader
    (`ota.bin`), `script.ver`, `blimit.bin` and `tail.bin`; the SDK's
    packaging adds the update loader as type 100 and `script.ver` (the
    packaging tool's version, `AC791N-v0.01-cfg_tool-v0.10` in the SDK)
    to the package before turning it into the update file.
  The emulator's package path reads only the header's CRC, the entry
  count and the first type-0 entry; a package for it needs no other
  entry. What the chip's updater needs is Q-26.

### HW-80: The FM-1's flash layout, and the region a firmware may use
- Fact: On an FM-1 with M-VAVE's firmware, the 1 MiB flash is laid out
  as follows (chip offsets):
  - `0x00000`-`0x03FFF`: the boot area: a header, the second-stage loader
    from `0x000A0` (which the mask ROM loads), the loader's configuration
    from `0x038D0`. Never erase or write it: the chip boots from it.
  - `0x04000`-`0x93FFF`: the app area: a file table, then the app and its
    configuration, encrypted with the chip's key (HW-81). The update
    package's flash image covers `0x00000`-`0x93FFF`.
  - `0x94000`-`0xE8FFF` (340 KiB): the stock firmware's key-value store
    ("VM"). The update path also stages its loader in "the VM/loader
    flash area" (FM-1-RE; where in it, not stated).
  - `0xE9000`-`0xE9FFF`: Bluetooth information ("BTIF").
  - `0xEA000`-`0xFBFFF` (72 KiB, 18 sectors): the stock firmware's user
    patch storage ("USR"); the update package carries a `USR` entry.
  - `0xFC000`-`0xFEFFF` (12 KiB): unused.
  - `0xFF000`-`0xFFFFF`: holds a per-unit key and address (`key_mac`).
    Never erase it: nothing can restore it. The SDK's packaging tool also
    reserves a flash's last 4 KiB by default.
  So a firmware's own storage must stay out of the boot area, out of its
  own image, and out of the last 4 KiB, and should stay out of the
  Bluetooth sector. In particular "the chip's last 64 KiB" includes the
  last sector: end a store at `0xFEFFF` at the latest. Where our firmware
  sits on the chip, and so what is free, is set when M9 packages it. Of
  the stock layout's regions past the app area: the USR region,
  `0xEA000`-`0xFBFFF` (72 KiB), holds the stock firmware's saved user
  patches, so a store there erases them, and the stock firmware reads that
  region back if the unit returns to it; `0xFC000`-`0xFEFFF` is unused
  but only 12 KiB (three sectors); the VM region is the stock firmware's
  settings and the update's staging area. Which one a store takes is a
  product choice, for the owner; keep it in one definition. FM-1-RE adds
  that its free regions have not been validated as safe for writes from
  outside the stock firmware, and whether an update rewrites the USR or
  VM region is not known (Q-24). In fwtest the whole chip past the image
  is erased and free (HW-5, HW-82).
- Sources: RE `docs/architecture.md` §2 ("Flash layout", from the update
  package's file table) and §3 (the mask ROM loads the loader from

/*
 * SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
 * SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
 *
 * The store (M7): our own record store in the flash chip's user region,
 * for the user patches, the patch selection and the settings
 * (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M7, has the design; docs/STORE-FORMAT.md the
 * bytes; tools/store.py reads and writes the same format).
 *
 * - The region is STORE_SECTORS sectors of 4 KiB, used as a ring: one
 *   sector at a time takes new records (the head); the others hold older
 *   ones. Each sector starts with a header holding its sequence number,
 *   one more than the sector used before it.
 * - A record holds a kind, an id (the slot), its payload's version, its
 *   length, a sequence number and a CRC-32 over all of it. Of the records
 *   with the same kind and id, the newest whose CRC holds is the one read.
 *   A record that fails is ignored, and so is anything else that is not
 *   erased: a sector is read whole, in 16-byte steps, and the head takes
 *   new records only after its last byte that is not erased.
 * - A write never changes a byte already written: a record is appended,
 *   so the previous copy stays readable until the new one is complete.
 * - When the head is full, the next sector in the ring becomes the head
 *   (erased first); the records still live in the sector after that, the
 *   oldest, are copied into the new head, so that sector holds nothing
 *   live by the time the ring comes round to erase it. Every sector is
 *   erased in turn: the wear is spread over the region.
 * - Main is the only caller: it reads at start-up (store_init, then
 *   store_get) and writes from its loop (store_put); the interrupts and
 *   core 1 never wait for the flash, and since M7 nothing runs from the
 *   code window (firmware/app.ld).
 * - Every flash access goes through SPI0 (HW-47); the window is never
 *   read for the store.
 * - Since clean-1027 (BR-9) kinds STORE_FW_KIND_FIRST to
 *   STORE_FW_KIND_LAST are kept for firmwares built on the base: any id
 *   (0 to 255), a payload of up to STORE_FW_MAX bytes, written as up to
 *   STORE_FW_PARTS records of STORE_FW_PART bytes (its parts) and read
 *   whole or not at all (below).
 * - Since BR-12 every save is atomic: cut short at any moment (power

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Phase A1's packager and reference reader of the update package, the
`.fwsc` (docs/A1-PLAN.md, Note A1-1), from docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-87 to
HW-93 only.

  fwsc.py pack APP.bin --version X.Y.Z --out FILE.fwsc [--identity ID]
      Packs the package link's raw image (tools/build.sh's app-pkg.bin,
      linked at 0x02000120, HW-91) into a package with one entry, the
      flash image: its flash header, a directory of two heads (the key
      block's and the app area's), our own key block, and the app area at
      flash 0x4000 with app.bin at 0x120 in it, scrambled with the key the
      key block gives (HW-88 to HW-90). The identity (the header blocks'
      markers) is small-beeps-<version> unless given. The same inputs
      give the same bytes (R-REPRO).
  fwsc.py FILE.fwsc [--unpack DIR]
      Runs fwtest's checks on a package, in fwtest's order
      (docs/HARNESS.md, "Packages"; HW-93), and prints what it found or
      the first check that failed (exit 1); --unpack writes the app
      (app.bin) and the flash image (flash.bin).
  fwsc.py broken APP.bin --out DIR
      Writes one broken package per check, DIR/<check>-<what>.fwsc, each
      failing that check and passing those before it (the tests').

What the facts leave open (Q-25, Q-26) the packager writes as 0, and the
reader checks nothing of: in the header, every field but its CRC and the
entry count (the list CRC and the image size: where, and over what, is
not given); in the entry, every field but its type, offset and length
(its name and CRC); in the flash header, the size for the programmer, the
VID, the file system's version, the alignment, the special options and
the PID (the flash size is written, 1 MiB, HW-77); in every directory
head, the reserved byte, and the attribute of the key block's head; in
the area head, every field but its length and its two CRCs. Data CRCs,
which nothing in the three load paths checks (HW-93), are our choice
where the facts don't say over which bytes: the key block's head's over
the key block and its CRC as stored (34 bytes); the app area's head (in
the flash directory) over the area as stored, scrambled; the area head's
over the rest of the area and app.bin's over the app, both plain. The
flash image covers the boot area and the app area only, so a package
writes nothing past the app area's end: not the stock user patch region
(0xEA000, HW-80), not the store (0xFC000). No loader is in it (HW-92,
HW-93; docs/A1-PLAN.md, "Loaders").
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import os
import struct
import sys

# HW-88: the header blocks, the logical header, the entries.
BLOCKS, BLOCK, BLOCK_DATA = 20, 48, 47
HEADER_FILE = BLOCKS * BLOCK                # 960 bytes of blocks
LOGICAL = BLOCKS * BLOCK_DATA               # 940 bytes of logical header
SHIFT = HEADER_FILE - LOGICAL               # logical n is file n + 20, n >= 940
END_MARK = 0x7D
HEADER_SIZE, ENTRY_SIZE = 64, 80
ENTRY_FLASH = 0
OTHER_BOARDS = ("SMK", "MKE", "STARRYKEY")  # an identity starting so is another board's
IDENTITY_MAX = 19
# Where the flash image starts in the file: past the header blocks, with
# zero bytes between, so the byte at file offset 1007 (where a 21st block's
# marker would sit, HW-88) is 0, not 0x7D, and no reader tries a longer
# header first.
DATA_FILE = 1024

# HW-87: the header key, the mask's seed.
HEADER_KEY = 0xFFFF

# HW-89: the flash image's heads.
HEAD = struct.Struct("<HHIIBBH16s")         # hdrcrc, datacrc, offset, length, attr, reserved, last, name
FLASH_HEAD = struct.Struct("<HH4sIBBBB16s")  # crc, size4burner, VID, flash size, fs version, align, reserved, options, PID
KEY_NAME = b"isd_config.ini"
AREA_NAME, AREA_ATTR = b"app_dir_head", 0x81
CHIP_BYTES = 0x100000                       # the FM-1's 1 MiB flash chip (HW-77)
KEY_BLOCK_AT = 0x60                         # right after the directory's two heads

# HW-90, HW-91: the app area, its directory, the app.
AREA = 0x4000

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH] [--define NAME]...
#                        [--demo plaits] [--src DIR]... [--leave-out FILE]...
#                        [--cflags DIR FLAGS]... [--cxxflags DIR FLAGS]...
#                        [--asflags DIR FLAGS]... [--platform] [--ld SCRIPT]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR;
#                                             --define adds -DNAME (test
#                                             builds, tools/perf.py; and a
#                                             firmware built on the base,
#                                             e.g. SB_ENGINE_EXTERNAL);
#                                             --demo builds a demo's own
#                                             image instead (M4b: the
#                                             Plaits load test), never the
#                                             firmware's; --src adds the
#                                             sources in a folder outside
#                                             firmware/, --leave-out
#                                             leaves a base source out
#                                             (since clean-1027, BR-5;
#                                             docs/BUILDING-ON-SMALL-BEEPS.md);
#                                             --cflags, --cxxflags and
#                                             --asflags add flags for the
#                                             C, C++ or assembly in a
#                                             --src folder or a folder in
#                                             one (since clean-1028, BR-11;
#                                             below);
#                                             --platform leaves the base's
#                                             instrument out (INSTRUMENT,
#                                             below) and links the platform
#                                             with the engine from --src
#                                             (BR-2), --ld with a script of
#                                             one's own that includes
#                                             platform.ld
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# The outputs: app.elf and app.bin (the raw image, linked at 0x02000000),
# app.size, and since A1 (not for --demo) app-pkg.elf and app-pkg.bin, the
# same objects linked at 0x02000120 for a .fwsc (tools/fwsc.py; HW-91).
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
#
# Sources from outside (--src DIR, BR-5): each folder is mounted read-only
# beside the source mount, at sb-src-N for the Nth (/mnt/sb-src-1 for
# build A), and built by its path from there (../sb-src-1/...), as the
# base's files are by theirs, so where it sits on the host never reaches
# an output. Every .c, .S and .cc under it is built, sorted
# by path, with the firmware's flags plus -I for the folder (C++ with the
# same CPU, warnings and freestanding flags, as C++14 without exceptions
# or RTTI), and named by its path (src<N>_<path>.o), so a name the base
# also uses is never mixed up with the base's. --leave-out FILE takes a
# base source (a path from the repository's root, under firmware/) out
# of the build, so a firmware can replace it or do without it. A
# firmware built on the base calls this script from the base's folder
# (docs/BUILDING-ON-SMALL-BEEPS.md).
#
# Per-folder flags (BR-11): --cflags DIR FLAGS adds FLAGS, after the
# base's own, to every C file under DIR, a --src folder or a folder in
# one; --cxxflags to its C++, --asflags to its assembly. Repeatable; a
# file under several such folders gets each one's flags in the order
# given (so a folder inside another can override it, -O2 after -O0, say).
# The base's own files, its runtime included, are always built with the
# base's flags. FLAGS are words of A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _ = + . , / : -;
# a relative path in -I, -isystem or -iquote (joined to it: -Iinclude)
# is from DIR. Only these families are taken: -D, -U, -O, -W, -w, -f,
# -m, -std=, -I, -isystem, -iquote, -g, -pedantic, -ansi; and of them
# not those that would reach the host, the outputs' determinism or
# another tool: an absolute path or one with "..", -fdebug-prefix-map
# and its kin, -fprofile..., -fplugin..., -fpass-plugin...,
# -fsave-optimization-record, -Wa, -Wp, -Wl (check_flags).
#
# The platform (BR-2): --platform leaves out the base's instrument, the
# files below, defines SB_ENGINE_EXTERNAL (firmware/src/engine.h) and
# links with firmware/platform.ld, whose assertions cover only the
# platform's records; --ld SCRIPT links with a script of one's own
# instead (in the base or in a --src folder), which includes platform.ld
# (INCLUDE platform.ld) and asserts its own records.
set -eu

INSTRUMENT="firmware/src/arp.c firmware/src/fm.c firmware/src/fm_play.c
            firmware/src/patches.c firmware/src/saving.c firmware/src/spectrum.c firmware/src/views.c"

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

# Refuses per-folder flags (BR-11) that could reach the host, make the
# outputs depend on where things are, or undo the build: only the
# families below are taken (above).
check_flags() {
    case "$2" in
        *[!A-Za-z0-9_=+.,/:\ -]*) echo "build: $1 '$2': flags are words of A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and _ = + . , / : -" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
    for w in $2; do
        case "$w" in
            /*|*=/*|-I/*|-isystem/*|-iquote/*|*..*)
                echo "build: $1 '$w': no absolute paths or .. (a path is from the folder)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
            -fdebug-prefix-map=*|-ffile-prefix-map=*|-fmacro-prefix-map=*|-fcoverage-prefix-map=*| \
            -fprofile*|-fplugin*|-fpass-plugin*|-fsave-optimization-record*|-Wa,*|-Wp,*|-Wl,*)
                echo "build: $1 '$w' is not one a folder may set" >&2; exit 2 ;;
            -D?*|-U?*|-O|-O?|-W?*|-w|-f?*|-m?*|-std=?*|-I?*|-isystem?*|-iquote?*|-g|-g0|-g1|-g2|-g3| \
            -pedantic|-pedantic-errors|-ansi) ;;
            *) echo "build: $1 '$w' is not one a folder may set (-D, -U, -O, -W, -w, -f, -m, -std=, -I, -isystem, -iquote, -g, -pedantic, -ansi)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src defines="" demo="" mounts="" srcs="" leave="" n=0
    platform="" ldscript="" ff=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --platform) platform=1; shift ;;
            --ld)
                [ -f "$2" ] || { echo "build: --ld $2: no such file" >&2; exit 2; }
                ldscript="$(cd "$(dirname "$2")" && pwd)/$(basename "$2")"; shift 2 ;;
            --src)

                [ -d "$2" ] || { echo "build: $1 $2 is not a folder" >&2; exit 2; }
                check_flags "$1" "$3"
                ff="$ff;${1#--}|$(cd "$2" && pwd)|$3"; shift 3 ;;
            --leave-out)
                case "$2" in
                    firmware/*) [ -f "$ROOT/$2" ] || { echo "build: --leave-out $2: no such base file" >&2; exit 2; } ;;
                    *) echo "build: --leave-out takes a base source's path from the repository's root (firmware/...)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                leave="$leave $2"; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --define)
                case "$2" in
                    ''|*[!A-Z0-9_]*) echo "build: --define takes a NAME of A-Z, 0-9 and _" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac

            --demo)
                case "$2" in
                    plaits) demo=$2 ;;
                    *) echo "build: --demo takes plaits" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac

    if [ -n "$platform" ]; then
        [ -z "$demo" ] || { echo "build: --platform and --demo don't go together" >&2; exit 2; }
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        leave="$leave $(echo $INSTRUMENT)"
        defines="$defines SB_ENGINE_EXTERNAL"
    fi
    # The linker script as the container sees it: from the source mount,
    # or from the outside folder (sb-src-N) that holds it.
    script=firmware/app.ld
    [ -z "$platform" ] || script=firmware/platform.ld
    if [ -n "$ldscript" ]; then
        script=""
        case "$ldscript" in
            "$ROOT"/*) script=${ldscript#"$ROOT"/} ;;
        esac

            n=$((n + 1))

                "$d"/*) script=../sb-src-$n/${ldscript#"$d"/} ;;
            esac

                -isystem?*) w=-isystem$m/${w#-isystem} ;;
                -iquote?*) w=-iquote$m/${w#-iquote} ;;
            esac
            g="$g $w"
        done
        folder_flags="$folder_flags;$k|$m|${g# }"
        IFS=';'
    done
    IFS=$old_ifs

    n=0 outside=""
    for d in $srcs; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        mounts="$mounts -v $d:$(dirname "$src_mount")/sb-src-$n:ro"
        outside="$outside $(dirname "$src_mount")/sb-src-$n"

        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e SB_DEFINES="$defines" -e SB_DEMO="$demo" \

# code (code and constants, in the image, wherever they run), data
# (initialised data: in the image and copied to RAM), bss (zeroed RAM, the
# beacon included), image (the raw image's length), stack (reserved at the
# top of RAM, both stacks), irq_stack (the lower part of it: the interrupt
# stack) and, since M7, ram_code (the part of code copied to RAM and run
# there, which takes RAM as data does).
write_size() {
    sym() { nm "$1" | awk -v s="$2" '$3 == s { print $1 }'; }
    hex() { printf '%d' "0x$1"; }
    origin=$(hex 02000000)
    data_load=$(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_load)")
    data=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_start)") ))
    bss=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_start)") ))
    stack=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    irq=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __irq_stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    ram_code=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __ram_code_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __ram_code_start)") ))
    printf 'code %d\ndata %d\nbss %d\nimage %d\nstack %d\nirq_stack %d\nram_code %d\n' \
        $((data_load - origin + ram_code)) $((data - ram_code)) "$bss" $((data_load - origin + data)) \
        "$stack" "$irq" "$ram_code"
}

# The Plaits demo's own sources and the vendored Plaits (M4b,
# docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md): our C glue and runtime with the firmware's flags;
# our C++ with the same warnings, as errors (Plaits' headers are system
# headers to it: their warnings are not ours to fix); the vendored files
# unmodified at upstream's -O2, with warnings off. All the C++ is built in
# upstream's portable configuration (-DTEST), with our standard headers
# and plaits_pre.h in place of a C library's. Objects are named after their
# paths, since vendored names repeat.
build_demo_plaits() {
    d=firmware/demos/plaits
    CXX="clang -target pi32v2 -x c++ -std=c++11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -fno-exceptions
         -fno-rtti -fno-threadsafe-statics -fno-common -g -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
         -I$d/include -Ifirmware/runtime/include -isystem vendor/plaits/eurorack -isystem vendor/plaits
         -I$d -Ifirmware/src
         -DTEST -include $d/include/plaits_pre.h"
    for d2 in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CXX="$CXX -D$d2"; done
    # PLAITS_HWFLOAT: the toolchain's hardware single-precision float
    # instructions (its fprev1 feature) instead of our soft-float, for the
    # C++ only: a measurement of what they would save, never the demo's
    # default, since whether the chip has them is open (SR-5).
    case " ${SB_DEFINES:-} " in
        *" PLAITS_HWFLOAT "*) CXX="$CXX -Xclang -target-feature -Xclang +fprev1" ;;
    esac
    defs=""
    for d2 in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do defs="$defs -D$d2"; done
    for s in $(find "$d" -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS $defs -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086,SC2046
            *) set -x; clang $(echo "$CFLAGS" | sed 's/ -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1//') -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    for s in $(find "$d" -name '*.cc' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.cc$/.o/')"
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        set -x; $CXX -Os -Wall -Wextra -Werror -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    for s in $(find vendor/plaits -name '*.cc' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.cc$/.o/')"
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        $CXX -O2 -w -c "$s" -o "$o"
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    echo "built $(find vendor/plaits -name '*.cc' | wc -l) vendored Plaits files"
}

# The flags of every folder holding the source $2 (its path from the
# source mount) given with option $1 (cflags, cxxflags or asflags), in
# the order given (BR-11; SB_FOLDER_FLAGS: entries "option|folder|flags",
# each after a ";").
folder_flags() {
    fl="" old_ifs=$IFS
    IFS=';'
    for e in ${SB_FOLDER_FLAGS:-}; do
        [ -n "$e" ] || continue
        k=${e%%|*} rest=${e#*|}
        d=${rest%%|*}
        [ "$k" = "$1" ] || continue
        case "$2" in
            "$d"/*) fl="$fl ${rest#*|}" ;;
        esac
    done
    IFS=$old_ifs
    echo "${fl# }"
}

# The sources of the folders given with --src (BR-5), mounted beside the
# source mount as sb-src-N: every .c, .S and .cc, sorted by path, named
# by it, and built by its path from the source mount.
build_outside() {
    k=0
    for m in ${SB_SRCS:-}; do
        k=$((k + 1))
        r=../sb-src-$k
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        for s in $(cd "$m" && find . -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' -o -name '*.cc' | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
            o="$obj/src${k}_$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/; s/\.cc$/.o/')"
            case "$s" in
                *.S) fl=$(folder_flags asflags "$r/$s"); set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -I"$r" $fl -c "$r/$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
                *.cc) fl=$(folder_flags cxxflags "$r/$s"); set -x; clang $CXXFLAGS -I"$r" $fl -c "$r/$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
                *) fl=$(folder_flags cflags "$r/$s")
                   set -x; clang $CFLAGS -Ifirmware/runtime/include -I"$r" $fl -c "$r/$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            esac
            objs="$objs $o"
        done
    done
}

# The platform's runtime (firmware/runtime/, BR-4): memcpy, memmove and
# memset, what C++ needs (cxx.cc) and soft-float, in an archive the link
# takes last, so an image gets only the members it calls (the firmware:
# none). Its C is built without the float instructions, as soft-float's
# must be (and as the Plaits demo's C always was).
build_runtime() {
    rt=""
    for s in $(find firmware/runtime -name '*.c' -o -name '*.cc' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/runtime_$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.c$/.o/; s/\.cc$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *.cc) set -x; clang $CXXFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086,SC2046
            *) set -x; clang $(echo "$CFLAGS" | sed 's/ -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1//') -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        rt="$rt $o"
    done
    rm -f "$obj/libsb_runtime.a"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ar rcD "$obj/libsb_runtime.a" $rt
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    # The chip's CPU model and its single-precision float instructions, as
    # the SDK builds for it (HW-62, since M5). The Plaits demo's own C is
    # built without them, as before (build_demo_plaits): its soft-float
    # test must exercise the soft-float routines, and `-mcpu=r3` on its
    # own already makes the compiler use the instructions.
    CPU="-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
            -Ifirmware/src -Ivendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -D$d"; done
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -nostdinc -Werror"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do ASFLAGS="$ASFLAGS -D$d"; done
    # C++ from outside folders (BR-5): the C flags' CPU, warnings and
    # freestanding build, C++14 without exceptions, RTTI or guarded
    # statics.
    CXXFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -x c++ -std=c++14 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
              -fno-common -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -fno-threadsafe-statics -Wall -Wextra -Werror
              -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=. -Ifirmware/src -Ifirmware/runtime/include"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -D$d"; done
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    # Objects are intermediate: kept out of the outputs.
    obj=/tmp/small-beeps-obj
    rm -rf "$obj" && mkdir -p "$obj"
    objs=""
    # The demo is an engine on the engine seam (firmware/src/engine.h).
    if [ -n "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -DSB_DEMO_PLAITS -DSB_ENGINE_EXTERNAL -Ifirmware/demos/plaits"
    fi
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        case " ${SB_LEAVE_OUT:-} " in
            *" $s "*) echo "left out: $s"; continue ;;
        esac
        o="$obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    if [ -n "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        build_demo_plaits
    fi
    build_outside
    build_runtime
    # No store that writes back into the register it stores (since
    # clean-1027; tools/ownbase.pl, R-BUILD-3): every object's code is
    # checked before anything is linked, so no image holds one. One
    # exception: the Plaits demo's measurement builds with the hardware
    # float instructions (PLAITS_HWFLOAT, which only fwtest ever runs),
    # where the compiler puts such stores in the vendored Plaits; there
    # they are listed and counted, not refused.
    wb=0
    for o in $objs $rt; do
        objdump -d "$o" | perl tools/ownbase.pl "$(basename "$o")" || wb=$((wb + 1))
    done
    if [ "$wb" -ne 0 ]; then
        case " ${SB_DEMO:-}:${SB_DEFINES:-} " in
            *plaits:*" PLAITS_HWFLOAT "*)
                echo "ownbase check: $wb objects with such stores (above), allowed in a PLAITS_HWFLOAT measurement build" ;;
            *)
                echo "FAIL: a store writes back into the register it stores (above; tools/ownbase.pl)" >&2
                exit 1 ;;
        esac
    fi
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -L firmware -T "${SB_LD:-firmware/app.ld}" \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs "$obj/libsb_runtime.a"
    # The raw image is the code, then the initial data, which app.ld loads
    # right after it. This objcopy takes one section at a time, and ld's
    # own binary output gets data addresses wrong, so the two are joined.
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app.elf" "$obj/text.bin"
    objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$obj/data.bin"
    cat "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin" > "$out/app.bin"
    # The package link (Phase A1, HW-91): the same objects, linked where a
    # package's app.bin runs, 0x120 past the window's start; its raw image
    # is what tools/fwsc.py packs into a .fwsc. Not for a demo.
    if [ -z "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error --defsym=IMAGE_ORIGIN=0x02000120 \
            -L firmware -T "${SB_LD:-firmware/app.ld}" -o "$out/app-pkg.elf" $objs "$obj/libsb_runtime.a"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app-pkg.elf" "$obj/pkg-text.bin"
        objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app-pkg.elf" "$obj/pkg-data.bin"
        cat "$obj/pkg-text.bin" "$obj/pkg-data.bin" > "$out/app-pkg.bin"
    fi
    set +x
    write_size "$out/app.elf" > "$out/app.size"
    cat "$out/app.size"
    image=$(awk '$1 == "image" { print $2 }' "$out/app.size")
    if [ "$(wc -c < "$out/app.bin")" -ne "$image" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: app.bin is not the $image bytes app.ld lays out" >&2; exit 1
    fi
    # Nothing in the firmware may depend on which link it is (A1-1): what
    # runs from RAM is byte for byte the same in both, the boot code (run
    # from the window) is as long, and the package's starts at 0x02000120.
    # The RAM check is the firmware's, not a test build's: the store's wipe
    # test (SB_TEST_STORE_WIPE) turns a link symbol into a chip offset.
    if [ -z "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        [ -n "${SB_DEFINES:-}" ] || cmp "$obj/data.bin" "$obj/pkg-data.bin" \
            || { echo "FAIL: the package link's RAM code and data differ from the raw image's" >&2; exit 1; }
        [ "$(wc -c < "$obj/pkg-text.bin")" -eq "$(wc -c < "$obj/text.bin")" ] \
            || { echo "FAIL: the package link's boot code is not as long as the raw image's" >&2; exit 1; }
        [ "$(nm "$out/app-pkg.elf" | awk '$3 == "_start" { print $1 }')" = 02000120 ] \
            || { echo "FAIL: the package link's _start is not at 0x02000120" >&2; exit 1; }
        rm "$obj/pkg-text.bin" "$obj/pkg-data.bin"
    fi
    rm "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin"
    # No output may contain the absolute source path, or an outside
    # folder's mount path.
    for f in $(find "$out" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        for p in "$src" ${SB_SRCS:-}; do
            if grep -q -F "$p" "$f"; then
                echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $p" >&2; exit 1
            fi
        done
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

toolUseResult.stdout:
--src)
                [ -d "$2" ] || { echo "build: --src $2 is not a folder" >&2; exit 2; }
                d=$(cd "$2" && pwd)
                case "$ROOT/" in
                    "$d"/*) echo "build: --src $2 holds the base itself; give the folders of your own sources" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                case "$d/" in
                    "$ROOT/firmware/"*) echo "build: --src $2 is inside firmware/, which is built already" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                    *" "*) echo "build: --src $2: a path with a space is not supported" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                n=$((n + 1))
                srcs="$srcs $d"
                shift 2 ;;
            --cflags|--cxxflags|--asflags)
                [ $# -ge 3 ] || { echo "build: $1 takes a folder and its flags" >&2; exit 2; }
                [ -d "$2" ] || { echo "build: $1 $2 is not a folder" >&2; exit 2; }
                check_flags "$1" "$3"
                ff="$ff;${1#--}|$(cd "$2" && pwd)|$3"; shift 3 ;;
            --leave-out)
                case "$2" in
                    firmware/*) [ -f "$ROOT/$2" ] || { echo "build: --leave-out $2: no such base file" >&2; exit 2; } ;;
                    *) echo "build: --leave-out takes a base source's path from the repository's root (firmware/...)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                leave="$leave $2"; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --define)
                case "$2" in
                    ''|*[!A-Z0-9_]*) echo "build: --define takes a NAME of A-Z, 0-9 and _" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                defines="$defines $2"; shift 2 ;;
            --demo)
                case "$2" in
                    plaits) demo=$2 ;;
                    *) echo "build: --demo takes plaits" >&2; exit 2 ;;
                esac
                shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "build: --out DIR is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    if [ -n "$platform" ]; then
        [ -z "$demo" ] || { echo "build: --platform and --demo don't go together" >&2; exit 2; }
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        leave="$leave $(echo $INSTRUMENT)"
        defines="$defines SB_ENGINE_EXTERNAL"
    fi
    # The linker script as the container sees it: from the source mount,
    # or from the outside folder (sb-src-N) that holds it.
    script=firmware/app.ld
    [ -z "$platform" ] || script=firmware/platform.ld
    if [ -n "$ldscript" ]; then
        script=""
        case "$ldscript" in
            "$ROOT"/*) script=${ldscript#"$ROOT"/} ;;
        esac
        n=0
        for d in $srcs; do
            n=$((n + 1))
            case "$ldscript" in
                "$d"/*) script=../sb-src-$n/${ldscript#"$d"/} ;;
            esac
        done
        [ -n "$script" ] || { echo "build: --ld must name a file in the base or in a --src folder" >&2; exit 2; }
    fi
    # Each folder's flags (BR-11), its folder as the container builds it
    # (../sb-src-N/...), and the paths in its -I, -isystem and -iquote
    # from it.
    folder_flags=""
    old_ifs=$IFS; IFS=';'
    for e in $ff; do
        [ -n "$e" ] || continue
        k=${e%%|*} rest=${e#*|}
        d=${rest%%|*} f=${rest#*|}
        m="" n=0
        IFS=$old_ifs
        for sd in $srcs; do
            n=$((n + 1))
            case "$d/" in
                "$sd"/*) m=../sb-src-$n${d#"$sd"} ;;
            esac
        done
        [ -n "$m" ] || { echo "build: --$k $d is not a --src folder or inside one" >&2; exit 2; }
        g=""
        for w in $f; do
            case "$w" in
                -I?*) w=-I$m/${w#-I} ;;
                -isystem?*) w=-isystem$m/${w#-isystem} ;;
                -iquote?*) w=-iquote$m/${w#-iquote} ;;
            esac
            g="$g $w"
        done
        folder_flags="$folder_flags;$k|$m|${g# }"
        IFS=';'
    done
    IFS=$old_ifs
    # The outside folders, beside the source mount (above).
    n=0 outside=""
    for d in $srcs; do
        n=$((n + 1))
        mounts="$mounts -v $d:$(dirname "$src_mount")/sb-src-$n:ro"
        outside="$outside $(dirname "$src_mount")/sb-src-$n"
    done
    tag=$(image_tag)
    docker image inspect "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cmd_image
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -e SB_DEFINES="$defines" -e SB_DEMO="$demo" \
        -e SB_SRCS="$outside" -e SB_LEAVE_OUT="$leave" -e SB_LD="$script" \
        -e SB_FOLDER_FLAGS="$folder_flags" \
        -v "$ROOT:$src_mount:ro" $mounts -v "$out:/out" -w "$src_mount" \
        "$tag" sh "$src_mount/tools/build.sh" inside "$src_mount" /out
    cat "$out/SHA256SUMS"
}

# The image's size in bytes, from the symbols firmware/app.ld defines:
# code (code and constants, in the image, wherever they run), data
# (initialised data: in the image and copied to RAM), bss (zeroed RAM, the
# beacon included), image (the raw image's length), stack (reserved at the
# top of RAM, both stacks), irq_stack (the lower part of it: the interrupt
# stack) and, since M7, ram_code (the part of code copied to RAM and run
# there, which takes RAM as data does).
write_size() {
    sym() { nm "$1" | awk -v s="$2" '$3 == s { print $1 }'; }
    hex() { printf '%d' "0x$1"; }
    origin=$(hex 02000000)
    data_load=$(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_load)")
    data=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __data_start)") ))
    bss=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __bss_start)") ))
    stack=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    irq=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __irq_stack_top)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __stack_limit)") ))
    ram_code=$(( $(hex "$(sym "$1" __ram_code_end)") - $(hex "$(sym "$1" __ram_code_start)") ))
    printf 'code %d\ndata %d\nbss %d\nimage %d\nstack %d\nirq_stack %d\nram_code %d\n' \
        $((data_load - origin + ram_code)) $((data - ram_code)) "$bss" $((data_load - origin + data)) \

# The flags of every folder holding the source $2 (its path from the
# source mount) given with option $1 (cflags, cxxflags or asflags), in
# the order given (BR-11; SB_FOLDER_FLAGS: entries "option|folder|flags",
# each after a ";").
folder_flags() {
    fl="" old_ifs=$IFS
    IFS=';'
    for e in ${SB_FOLDER_FLAGS:-}; do
        [ -n "$e" ] || continue
        k=${e%%|*} rest=${e#*|}
        d=${rest%%|*}
        [ "$k" = "$1" ] || continue
        case "$2" in
            "$d"/*) fl="$fl ${rest#*|}" ;;
        esac
    done
    IFS=$old_ifs
    echo "${fl# }"
}

# The sources of the folders given with --src (BR-5), mounted beside the
# source mount as sb-src-N: every .c, .S and .cc, sorted by path, named
# by it, and built by its path from the source mount.
build_outside() {
    k=0
    for m in ${SB_SRCS:-}; do
        k=$((k + 1))
        r=../sb-src-$k
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        for s in $(cd "$m" && find . -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' -o -name '*.cc' | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
            o="$obj/src${k}_$(echo "$s" | tr / _ | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/; s/\.cc$/.o/')"
            case "$s" in
                *.S) fl=$(folder_flags asflags "$r/$s"); set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -I"$r" $fl -c "$r/$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
                *.cc) fl=$(folder_flags cxxflags "$r/$s"); set -x; clang $CXXFLAGS -I"$r" $fl -c "$r/$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
                *) fl=$(folder_flags cflags "$r/$s")
                   set -x; clang $CFLAGS -Ifirmware/runtime/include -I"$r" $fl -c "$r/$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            esac
            objs="$objs $o"
        done
    done
}

# The platform's runtime (firmware/runtime/, BR-4): memcpy, memmove and
# memset, what C++ needs (cxx.cc) and soft-float, in an archive the link
# takes last, so an image gets only the members it calls (the firmware:
# none). Its C is built without the float instructions, as soft-float's
# must be (and as the Plaits demo's C always was).
build_runtime() {
    rt=""
    for s in $(find firmware/runtime -name '*.c' -o -name '*.cc' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        o="$obj/runtime_$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.c$/.o/; s/\.cc$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *.cc) set -x; clang $CXXFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086,SC2046
            *) set -x; clang $(echo "$CFLAGS" | sed 's/ -mcpu=r3 -mfprev1//') -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        rt="$rt $o"
    done
    rm -f "$obj/libsb_runtime.a"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ar rcD "$obj/libsb_runtime.a" $rt
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    # The chip's CPU model and its single-precision float instructions, as
    # the SDK builds for it (HW-62, since M5). The Plaits demo's own C is
    # built without them, as before (build_demo_plaits): its soft-float
    # test must exercise the soft-float routines, and `-mcpu=r3` on its
    # own already makes the compiler use the instructions.
    CPU="-mcpu=r3 -mfprev1"
    # -nostdinc: no C library headers either; the SDK's register headers
    # are the only outside includes. -fno-common puts zeroed data in .bss.
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
            -fno-common -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=.
            -Ifirmware/src -Ivendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -D$d"; done
    # Assembly is built without -g, which would record the source path.
    ASFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -nostdinc -Werror"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do ASFLAGS="$ASFLAGS -D$d"; done
    # C++ from outside folders (BR-5): the C flags' CPU, warnings and
    # freestanding build, C++14 without exceptions, RTTI or guarded
    # statics.
    CXXFLAGS="-target pi32v2 $CPU -x c++ -std=c++14 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -nostdinc -Os -g
              -fno-common -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti -fno-threadsafe-statics -Wall -Wextra -Werror
              -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=. -Ifirmware/src -Ifirmware/runtime/include"
    for d in ${SB_DEFINES:-}; do CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS -D$d"; done
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    # Objects are intermediate: kept out of the outputs.
    obj=/tmp/small-beeps-obj
    rm -rf "$obj" && mkdir -p "$obj"
    objs=""
    # The demo is an engine on the engine seam (firmware/src/engine.h).
    if [ -n "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -DSB_DEMO_PLAITS -DSB_ENGINE_EXTERNAL -Ifirmware/demos/plaits"
    fi
    for s in $(find firmware/src -name '*.c' -o -name '*.S' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        case " ${SB_LEAVE_OUT:-} " in
            *" $s "*) echo "left out: $s"; continue ;;
        esac
        o="$obj/$(basename "$s" | sed 's/\.[cS]$/.o/')"
        case "$s" in
            *.S) set -x; clang $ASFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
            # shellcheck disable=SC2086
            *) set -x; clang $CFLAGS -c "$s" -o "$o"; set +x ;;
        esac
        objs="$objs $o"
    done
    if [ -n "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        build_demo_plaits
    fi
    build_outside
    build_runtime
    # No store that writes back into the register it stores (since
    # clean-1027; tools/ownbase.pl, R-BUILD-3): every object's code is
    # checked before anything is linked, so no image holds one. One
    # exception: the Plaits demo's measurement builds with the hardware
    # float instructions (PLAITS_HWFLOAT, which only fwtest ever runs),
    # where the compiler puts such stores in the vendored Plaits; there
    # they are listed and counted, not refused.
    wb=0
    for o in $objs $rt; do
        objdump -d "$o" | perl tools/ownbase.pl "$(basename "$o")" || wb=$((wb + 1))
    done
    if [ "$wb" -ne 0 ]; then
        case " ${SB_DEMO:-}:${SB_DEFINES:-} " in
            *plaits:*" PLAITS_HWFLOAT "*)
                echo "ownbase check: $wb objects with such stores (above), allowed in a PLAITS_HWFLOAT measurement build" ;;
            *)
                echo "FAIL: a store writes back into the register it stores (above; tools/ownbase.pl)" >&2
                exit 1 ;;
        esac
    fi
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error -L firmware -T "${SB_LD:-firmware/app.ld}" \
        -o "$out/app.elf" $objs "$obj/libsb_runtime.a"
    # The raw image is the code, then the initial data, which app.ld loads
    # right after it. This objcopy takes one section at a time, and ld's
    # own binary output gets data addresses wrong, so the two are joined.
    objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app.elf" "$obj/text.bin"
    objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app.elf" "$obj/data.bin"
    cat "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin" > "$out/app.bin"
    # The package link (Phase A1, HW-91): the same objects, linked where a
    # package's app.bin runs, 0x120 past the window's start; its raw image
    # is what tools/fwsc.py packs into a .fwsc. Not for a demo.
    if [ -z "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        ld -nostdlib --no-undefined --orphan-handling=error --defsym=IMAGE_ORIGIN=0x02000120 \
            -L firmware -T "${SB_LD:-firmware/app.ld}" -o "$out/app-pkg.elf" $objs "$obj/libsb_runtime.a"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/app-pkg.elf" "$obj/pkg-text.bin"
        objcopy -O binary -j .data "$out/app-pkg.elf" "$obj/pkg-data.bin"
        cat "$obj/pkg-text.bin" "$obj/pkg-data.bin" > "$out/app-pkg.bin"
    fi
    set +x
    write_size "$out/app.elf" > "$out/app.size"
    cat "$out/app.size"
    image=$(awk '$1 == "image" { print $2 }' "$out/app.size")
    if [ "$(wc -c < "$out/app.bin")" -ne "$image" ]; then
        echo "FAIL: app.bin is not the $image bytes app.ld lays out" >&2; exit 1
    fi
    # Nothing in the firmware may depend on which link it is (A1-1): what
    # runs from RAM is byte for byte the same in both, the boot code (run
    # from the window) is as long, and the package's starts at 0x02000120.
    # The RAM check is the firmware's, not a test build's: the store's wipe
    # test (SB_TEST_STORE_WIPE) turns a link symbol into a chip offset.
    if [ -z "${SB_DEMO:-}" ]; then
        [ -n "${SB_DEFINES:-}" ] || cmp "$obj/data.bin" "$obj/pkg-data.bin" \
            || { echo "FAIL: the package link's RAM code and data differ from the raw image's" >&2; exit 1; }
        [ "$(wc -c < "$obj/pkg-text.bin")" -eq "$(wc -c < "$obj/text.bin")" ] \
            || { echo "FAIL: the package link's boot code is not as long as the raw image's" >&2; exit 1; }
        [ "$(nm "$out/app-pkg.elf" | awk '$3 == "_start" { print $1 }')" = 02000120 ] \
            || { echo "FAIL: the package link's _start is not at 0x02000120" >&2; exit 1; }
        rm "$obj/pkg-text.bin" "$obj/pkg-data.bin"
    fi
    rm "$obj/text.bin" "$obj/data.bin"
    # No output may contain the absolute source path, or an outside
    # folder's mount path.
    for f in $(find "$out" -type f | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        for p in "$src" ${SB_SRCS:-}; do
            if grep -q -F "$p" "$f"; then
                echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $p" >&2; exit 1
            fi
        done
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

import os
import subprocess
import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT

SAMPLE = """
t.o:\tfile format ELF32-pi32v2

Disassembly of section .text:
f:
       0:    d9 e8 20 00       \t[--sp] = {rets, r5}
       4:    d0 ec 17 10       \t[++r1=4] = r1
       8:    a2 05             \t[r2++=4] = r2
       a:    dc ee 31 34       \tb[++r3=r4] = r3
       e:    dd 06             \th[r5++=-2] = r5
      10:    a3 05             \t[r2++=4] = r3
Disassembly of section .text.g:
g:
      20:    a3 05             \tr1 = [r1++=4]
      22:    a3 05             \t[r12+4] = r12
      24:    a3 05             \t[r1++=4] = r10 #
      26:    a3 05             \t[r1+r2] = r1
      28:    a3 05             \th[++r7=2] = r7 #
"""


class OwnBaseTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-BUILD-3"""

    def run_check(self, text):
        p = subprocess.run(["perl", os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "ownbase.pl"), "t.o"],
                           input=text.encode(), stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout.decode().splitlines()

    def test_flags_each_store_into_its_own_base_register_with_its_place(self):
        rc, lines = self.run_check(SAMPLE)
        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
        self.assertEqual(lines, [
            "t.o: f+0x4 (.text): [++r1=4] = r1",
            "t.o: f+0x8 (.text): [r2++=4] = r2",
            "t.o: f+0xa (.text): b[++r3=r4] = r3",
            "t.o: f+0xe (.text): h[r5++=-2] = r5",
            "t.o: g+0x8 (.text.g): h[++r7=2] = r7 #",
        ])

    def test_passes_code_without_one(self):
        rc, lines = self.run_check("Disassembly of section .text:\nf:\n   0:  a3 05  \t[r2++=4] = r3\n")
        self.assertEqual((rc, lines), (0, []))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""The store's format (docs/STORE-FORMAT.md; firmware/src/store.c, M7):
reads a flash image as the firmware does, and writes one as the firmware
would, for the tests (tools/fw-suite.py) and for people.

  store.py show FLASH.bin      what the store in a flash image holds

The reader follows store.c's rules exactly: the valid sector with the
highest sequence number is the head; every valid sector is read whole in
16-byte steps; a block that is erased or fails is skipped; of the records
with the same key the newest valid one counts, and a reset voids every
record older than it. The writer (Store) appends the same way, including
the ring's compaction, so an image it makes is one the firmware could
have made; Store.raw_record writes anywhere, for images it never would.

Since clean-1027 (BR-9; docs/STORE-FORMAT.md, "Kinds for firmwares built
on the base") kinds FW_KIND_FIRST to FW_KIND_LAST are kept for firmwares
built on the base: a payload of up to FW_MAX bytes, written as up to
FW_PARTS records (its parts), read whole or not at all (Image.get_fw,
Store.put_fw), voided by a reset as every other kind.
"""

import struct
import sys
import zlib

CHIP = 0x100000
REGION_END = 0xFF000           # the region ends where the per-unit last sector begins (HW-80)
USER_REGION = (0xEA000, 0xFC000)   # the stock firmware's saved patches (HW-80): never touched
SECTOR = 4096
SECTORS = 3                    # today's region: 0xFC000 to 0xFEFFF
SIZE = SECTORS * SECTOR
WIDE_SECTORS = 5               # the wide region test build's (SB_TEST_STORE_WIDE; BR-12)
PAGE = 256
BLOCK = 16
HEADER = 12
MAX_PAYLOAD = 112
SECTOR_MAGIC = 0x31534253
FORMAT = 1
RECORD_MAGIC = 0xA5
CUT_PARAM = 0xE8000            # the power cut test build's two words (store.c)

SLOTS = 16
KIND_NAMES = {PATCH: "patch", SELECTION: "selection", SETTINGS: "settings", RESET: "reset"}

# Kinds for firmwares built on the base (BR-9; store.h): any id, a payload
# in parts, each part's payload a 4-byte tag (the sequence number of the
# write's first part) and up to PART_DATA bytes of the payload.
FW_KIND_FIRST, FW_KIND_LAST = 0x80, 0xFE
TAG = 4
PART_DATA = 492
PART_MAX = TAG + PART_DATA       # a part's payload: its record is 512 bytes
FW_PARTS = 12
FW_MAX = FW_PARTS * PART_DATA     # 5 904 bytes, more than the region can hold beside anything
FW_KEYS = 32                      # parts the store keeps track of at once
FW_PAYLOADS = 32                  # payloads the store keeps track of at once (since BR-12)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""The tests of the seams for firmwares built on small-beeps (clean-1027;
docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, "Seams for firmwares built on small-beeps";
docs/BUILDING-ON-SMALL-BEEPS.md), check C-SEAMS.

  seams_suite.py --build DIR --out DIR [--only NAME ...]

DIR is build A's outputs (tools/build.sh build). Each case builds what it
needs with tools/build.sh into OUT/<case>/ and runs it in fwtest
(tools/fwtest, the pinned image) where it runs anything. The cases:

- ownbase (R-BUILD-3): a test build holding a store that writes back
  into the register it stores (SB_TEST_OWNBASE, firmware/src/probe.c)
  is refused, its message naming the object, the function and the
  instruction, and so is the same with PLAITS_HWFLOAT defined (the
  check's one exception is the Plaits demo's hardware-float measurement
  builds, tools/build.sh); build A, which passed the same check, holds
  none.

- outside (R-BUILD-4): the firmware built with an outside source folder
  (tools/build.sh --src tests/seams/outside: C including a base header
  and one of its own, assembly in a folder below, C++, and a file named
  as a base file is): each one's symbols in the ELF, the base's
  same-named file built too; the folder copied to two other places on
  the host and built from each, with the source mounted at another path
  for one (as C-BUILD-B does), gives the same outputs byte for byte;
  --leave-out firmware/src/probe.c builds without it (its object never
  built) and, as it holds nothing without a test define, gives build A's
  image; a folder holding the base, a folder inside firmware/ and a base
  file that isn't one are refused.

- flags (R-BUILD-5): per-folder compiler flags (BR-11). The firmware
  built with tests/seams/flags as --src, its C given -DSB_FLAGS_OUTER=7
  -O2 (--cflags), its folder inner/ -DSB_FLAGS_INNER=5 -Iinclude as
  well, its C++ -DSB_FLAGS_CXX=2 (--cxxflags) and its assembly
  -DSB_FLAGS_ASM (--asflags): each file builds only with its folders'
  flags (each #errors otherwise; the -O2 after the base's -Os, the outer
  folder's before the inner's, -Iinclude from inner/), its symbol in the
  ELF; the base's own files' compile lines carry none of them and are
  the lines of the same build without the flags (of firmware/src/,
  which come before the folder's files stop it); the folder copied to two other places and built from
  each, one with the source mounted elsewhere, gives the same bytes; and
  refused: a folder not inside a --src folder, a base folder, an
  absolute path, "..", -fdebug-prefix-map, -o, -Xclang, -Wp, an @file, a
  bare -isystem, and a folder without its flags.
- engine (R-ENG-1): the engine seam. A test engine from outside
  firmware/ (tests/seams/engine/, built with SB_ENGINE_EXTERNAL) runs in
  fwtest for 2.3 s with two key taps (tests/seams/scripts/engine.txt):
  its record (read by its ELF symbol) shows its init called once, before
  the tick's interrupts and the audio started; every audio block given
  to its block callback (as many as the audio record counts, 64 frames
  each); its serve called before the loop and on the wakes (the two
  whole seconds, the taps), seeing both taps its block callback took;
  its square wave in the audio, with no underrun; and the base's
  instrument never started (the FM engine's record still zero). The
  Plaits demo is an engine on the same seam (C-PLAITS-BENCH).
- platform (R-PLAT-1): the same test engine linked with the platform
  alone (tools/build.sh --platform, with its own script,
  tests/seams/engine/engine.ld, that includes firmware/platform.ld and
  asserts its record first among the engine's records, 0x01C00870):
  none of the instrument's functions or records in the ELF, the
  platform's records where the base has them, the package link built
  too, and the engine case's run and checks pass on it (the engine's
  slot, where the base keeps its FM engine's record, still zero).
- core 1 (R-CORE-1), within engine and platform: since BR-3 the test
  engine starts core 1 with sb_core1_start (core1.h) and hands it a job
  every block with sb_publish and sb_shared: core 1 starts (1), does one
  job a block, every answer right and in time, and source 126's vector
  word, borrowed for core 1's start, holds its stub again; with the
  platform alone too.
- runtime (R-RT-1), within engine and platform: since BR-4 the test
  engine's init runs C++ needing the platform's runtime
  (tests/seams/engine/sb_test_runtime.cc: a virtual class, std::sort,
  memcpy, memmove and memset with lengths known at run time, a static
  object whose constructor main() runs, and one with a destructor) and
  records its result, 1301; the runtime's members are in the ELF; and build A,
  which calls none of them, has none (the archive gives an image only
  what it calls).
- sysex (R-MIDI-8): MIDI in's SysEx tap, on the test engine linked with
  the platform alone. Its script, written here: a System Exclusive
  message of SYSEX_DATA (4 104) data bytes, sent in lines of 60 every
  20 ms (fwtest drops bytes when more than about a second's worth wait),
  with a clock byte (F8) in its middle; then one cut short by a note on.
  The tap sees both begin, every data byte in order and no other
  (length, sum by place, first and last, against the script's), the
  first end with F7 and the second cut by 0x90; the work runs in the
  serve; midi_read hands on the clock and the note; MIDI's record counts
  the first message long (past MIDI_SYSEX_LIMIT) and no byte is dropped.
- rawout (R-MIDIOUT-9): MIDI out's raw bytes, on the same build. At the
  first whole second the test engine's serve hands MIDI out a System
  Exclusive message of RAW_LEN (600) bytes; for 300 blocks from then its
  block callback queues a clock every block and a note on or off every
  16th (no more than the queue holds while the stream runs). On the wire
  (fwtest's --midi-out): the 600 bytes in order, nothing inside them but
  clocks (at least one, so a clock waits for no stream), every note
  after the F7, the first carrying its status, all of them and every
  clock sent, none dropped; the stream counted whole and the serve
  finding it gone.
- store (R-STORE-10): the store's kinds for firmwares built on the base,
  on the same build, in runs chained through the flash file
  (tools/store.py writes a control record before each, which the test
  engine reads at start-up and acts on in its first serve): a 4 096-byte
  payload and a small one written and read back, then read at the next
  start-up; since BR-12 a rewrite, which needs room for both copies, is
  refused as full in today's region, nothing written and the old payload
  kept; a factory reset voids both; then, alone in the store, 5 000
  bytes written and read back and the store's largest payload
  (STORE_FW_MAX) refused as full. After every run tools/store.py's
  reader finds what the firmware does.
- powercut (R-STORE-11): BR-12's saves that survive a power cut. Four
  saves, three of them from the base's full store (16 user slots, the
  selection, the settings) beside the firmware kinds' payloads, started by a key
  tap (tests/seams/engine's steps 0x80 and up): a 4 096-byte payload
  rewritten on the wide region test build (SB_TEST_STORE_WIDE, 5
  sectors); on today's region a 3 400-byte payload rewritten where the
  ring must copy the old write's parts forward during the rewrite (the
  case checks it did), a one-part payload rewritten (300 bytes) and a
  user slot's patch, these two with the head full, so that each takes a
  new sector and compacts. A run with --flash-log gives the
  save's flash commands; then for each command a power cut (fwtest's
