`STORE_ERR_FULL` past what fits, before writing anything, and what was
there stays. For more, choose a larger region (below). `store_reset()`
voids everything (a factory reset). docs/STORE-FORMAT.md has the bytes.

**Where the store goes.** The store's region is yours to choose (R-STORE-12).
By default it is the three sectors at `0xFC000` to `0xFEFFF`, which the
stock layout leaves unused (HW-80); the stock firmware's user patch
region below it (`0xEA000` to `0xFBFFF`) is never touched. To choose
another, set the symbol pair `STORE_BASE` (a chip offset) and
`STORE_SIZE` (bytes) in your linker script, before it includes the
platform's:

```
/* src/my.ld */
STORE_BASE = 0x84000;     /* 16 sectors, 0x84000 to 0x93FFF */
STORE_SIZE = 0x10000;

INCLUDE platform.ld

ASSERT(my_record == 0x01C00870, "my record must follow the store's")
```

The store's code is the same in any region; it reads the pair as link
symbols (`sb_store_base` and `sb_store_size`, which `nm app.elf` shows).
The build checks the region on both links (the raw image and the
package's, whose image is 0x120 bytes longer) and prints it:

```
app-pkg.elf: store region 0x84000 to 0x93FFF, 16 sectors (the image ends at 0x1F8E7)
```

It refuses a region, saying what is wrong and where one of that size
would fit, if it:

- doesn't start on a 4 KiB sector boundary, or isn't whole sectors;
- is smaller than 3 sectors (the store's minimum) or larger than 128
  (`STORE_SECTORS_MAX`, what the store keeps track of);
- overlaps your image (it starts at chip offset `0x4000`), or the boot
  area below it;
- crosses the end of the app area at `0x94000`, or lies past it in the
  stock layout: the VM region (`0x94000` to `0xE8FFF`), the Bluetooth
  sector, the stock user patch region, or the chip's last sector (its
  per-unit key, which must never be erased).

So a region goes either in the app area after your image, or in the
unused three sectors. `0x94000` is where the stock layout's app area
ends (HW-80); the hardware facts give the app area's start but no fixed
end, so this is the conservative reading until SR-11 is answered. For
example:

```
app.elf: store region: the region (0x10000 to 0x14FFF) overlaps the image, which ends at chip offset 0x1F8E7: start it at 0x20000 or later
app.elf: store region: where it would fit: a region of 5 sectors fits in the app area after the image, from 0x20000 to 0x8F000 at the latest; the unused region 0xFC000 to 0xFEFFF holds 3 (the default, STORE_BASE 0xFC000, STORE_SIZE 0x3000)
FAIL: the store's region doesn't fit (above; tools/store-region.pl)
```

How large: saves are atomic, so a rewrite needs room for the old payload
and the new one beside everything else live. The rule: everything live
plus the new payload's records must fit in the region's sectors but one
(the ring keeps one free to move on), each sector holding 4 080 bytes
of records, a part's record (512 bytes for a full one) never split
across two; a 4 096-byte payload is 9 parts, 4 288 bytes as records. In
practice, from the store's model (`tools/store.py`) over random
histories:

| Region | One payload, alone: the largest | Beside the base's full store | 4 096-byte payloads, each rewritable |
|-------:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 3 sectors (the default) | 3 920 bytes | 2 444 bytes | none |
| 4 sectors | 5 396 | 4 284 | 1 |
| 5 sectors | 5 904 (the most a payload takes) | 5 904 | 2 |
| 16 sectors | 5 904 | 5 904 | 12 (11 beside the base's full store) |

**A worked example: 16 sectors for several 4 096-byte records.** Say your
firmware keeps eight 4 096-byte records (kinds `0x80`, ids 0 to 7: a
bank of samples, say) and rewrites any of them at any time. Today's
three sectors can't rewrite even one. Sixteen sectors (64 KiB) keep
twelve, each rewritable, so eight leaves room to grow. Put them where
your image can grow into the space below them: the highest place in the
app area, `0x84000` to `0x93FFF` (the script above), leaves your image
room to grow to 512 KiB (`0x4000` to `0x83FFF`); the build will refuse
it the day the image reaches the store. Everything else is as before:

```c
for (id = 0; id < 8; id++)
    n = store_get(0x80, id, rec, sizeof rec, &version);   /* at start-up */
r = store_put(0x80, id, 1, rec, 4096);                    /* from your serve */
```

A larger region costs a little: start-up reads every sector (16 sectors
take about 1.4 ms, against 0.3 ms for three; measured in fwtest), and a
save in a nearly full region may move the ring on several sectors (an

### 2026-10-28 clean-store-region: each firmware chooses its own store region (R-STORE-12)

- **What.** The owner's answer to where a larger store goes (BR-9 and
  BR-12 left it open): small-beeps keeps today's three sectors at
  `0xFC000` as its default, the stock firmware's user patch region below
  them untouched (M8a's promise), and a firmware built on the base sets
  its own region's start and size in its linker settings, for example a
  larger region in the flash its own image's app area spans.
- **One definition, at link time.** `firmware/platform.ld` sets
  `STORE_BASE` and `STORE_SIZE` (chip offsets, bytes) with `DEFINED()`
  defaults, so a firmware's own script sets them first and includes the
  platform's (BUILDING-ON-SMALL-BEEPS.md, "Where the store goes"; ld
  2.26 takes a symbol its including script assigned before the
  `INCLUDE`, and `--defsym` too). The store reads them as link symbols,
  `sb_store_base` and `sb_store_size`, so one compiled `store.c` runs in
  any region: no define, no rebuild of the base's objects per firmware.
  `store.h`'s `STORE_BASE` and `STORE_SIZE` were constants (and
  `SB_TEST_STORE_WIDE` a second pair for a test build); they are the
  symbols' addresses now. The tables sized by sectors take
  `STORE_SECTORS_MAX` (128, 512 KiB, more than the app area can hold
  after any image; 768 bytes of RAM), and a sector's "holds a firmware
  kind" flag, a 32-bit mask until now (32 sectors at most), is a byte a
  sector. The ring's next sector is a compare, not a modulo (no divide at
  run time). The test engine's linker scripts `store5.ld` and
  `store16.ld` are the documented way, used.
- **The build refuses what doesn't fit** (`tools/store-region.pl`, run by
  `tools/build.sh` on both links, `app.elf` and `app-pkg.elf`, whose
  image is the longer by the app area's 0x120-byte directory): a start
  off a 4 KiB sector boundary or a size not whole sectors; fewer than 3
  sectors (the store's minimum: a head, a sector to move on to, and one
  to compact) or more than `STORE_SECTORS_MAX`; a region over the image
  (window address `0x02000000 + n` is chip offset `0x4000 + n`, HW-5,
  HW-91) or the boot area; a region across the app area's end, or in the
  stock layout past it (the VM region, the Bluetooth sector, the stock
  user patch region, the per-unit last sector: HW-80). Each message says
  what is wrong, with the numbers, and where a region of that size would
  fit (from the first sector after the image to the last start that ends
  by the app area's end, and the unused region's 3 sectors). The checks
  are in a script, not ld `ASSERT`s, because an `ASSERT`'s message can't
  carry numbers, and an `ASSERT` would stop the link before the script
  could say more; platform.ld's two store asserts are gone.
- **Stricter than asked, where HW-80 says so.** The owner named five
  refusals (over the image, across the app area's end, the stock user
  patch region, off a sector boundary, below the store's minimum). The
  build also refuses: more than the store keeps track of (an array
  bound, so a must), the boot area, and the stock layout's regions past
  the app area that aren't the unused one, the VM region (the stock
  firmware's settings, and where an update stages its loader), the
  Bluetooth sector and the last sector (never to be erased). HW-80 says a
  store "must stay out of" or "should stay out of" each.
- **Where the app area ends: a reading, SR-11.** HW-87 to HW-93 give the
  app area's start (`0x4000`) and its length as its area head says (our
  packager's: our app's), not a fixed end; HW-80 gives the stock
  layout's, `0x93FFF`. The build takes `0x94000` as the end, the most
  conservative reading that leaves the owner's example (a region in the
  space a stock image would take, after our smaller one) possible.
  SR-11 asks the spec side where the area may end, whether the chip's
  loader or an update touches flash past our package's image, and
  whether the window's decryption reaches there.
- **The store's room-making moves on more than once.** With the region
  free, the worked example (16 sectors for several 4 096-byte records)
  showed what bigger regions need. The ring made room by moving the head
  on once: open the next sector, copy the live records of the one after
  it into it (compaction), and, if what was left was still too small,
  refuse. With large payloads most sectors are mostly live, so one move
  often frees nothing: in the model, 16 sectors kept only one rewritable
  4 096-byte payload beside the base's full store in every history (two
  alone), though they have room for twelve. `make_room` (and the model's
  `_room`) now moves on while the new head has no room, once round the
  ring at most, each move an erase of a sector holding nothing live and
  a copy of the next's live records, as before; still `STORE_ERR_FULL`
  when the sector to move to holds something live. A save that one move
  served makes exactly the commands it made before (the loop only goes
  on where the old code refused), so every history the store took before
  is unchanged. The cost: in a nearly full region one save can erase
  several sectors (in the power-cut case's save, 2 for one part; up to 7
  seen in the model's searches), still spread over the ring.
- **More parts kept track of.** `STORE_FW_KEYS`, the places for parts,
  was 32: three 4 096-byte payloads (9 parts each) left no room for a
  rewrite of one, in any region. It is 128 (1.5 KiB more RAM): 14 such
  payloads, 13 beside a rewrite. Past it a write is refused as full, as
  before. `STORE_FW_PAYLOADS` (32 payloads) stays.
- **The sizing rule, plainly.** A rewrite is atomic (BR-12), so it needs
  room for the old payload and the new one at once: everything live plus
  the new payload's records must fit in the region's sectors but one, at
  4 080 bytes of records a sector (`(STORE_SECTORS - 1) * 4 080`, the
  check `put_fw` makes before writing anything), with no record across
  two sectors, and its parts within the places for parts. A payload of
  n bytes is `ceil(n / 492)` parts of 512 bytes as records (the last
  smaller); 4 096 bytes take 4 288. The ring's layout takes some of that
  room back, so what fits in every history is less; from the model
  (`tools/store.py`), the same histories as clean-1028's table, which
  this session's script reproduces on main's model (3 920, 1 664 and
  never in 3 sectors; 4 904, 3 268 and never in 4; 5 904, 4 948 and
  always in 5):

  | Region | One payload alone, rewritten 40 times | One payload beside the base's full store and a small payload (100 histories) | A 4 096-byte payload beside the base's full store (300 histories) | 4 096-byte payloads, each rewritable: alone (beside the base's full store; 100 histories in 16 sectors, 300 in 5) |
  |-------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|
  | 3 sectors (the default) | 3 920 bytes | 2 444 bytes (1 664 before) | never | none |
  | 4 sectors | 5 396 (4 904) | 4 284 (3 268) | every one (never) | 1 (1) |
  | 5 sectors | 5 904 | 5 904 (4 948) | every one | 2 (2) (1 (1) before) |
  | 16 sectors | 5 904 | 5 904 | every one | 12 (11) (2 (1) before) |

  So a 4 096-byte payload now needs 4 sectors beside the base's full
  store, where clean-1028 found 5. The store's format is unchanged
  (docs/STORE-FORMAT.md): a region of any size from 3 sectors up is the
  same ring of the same sectors.
- **Tested.** C-UNIT: `tests/test_store_region.py`, each refusal on the
  check's own input (the symbols `nm` prints), with its message and the
  place it offers, the default and both test regions taken, every
  problem of a region listed; `tests/test_store.py`, the model in 5 and
  16 sectors from `0x20000`: a 4 096-byte rewrite beside the base's full
  store cut at every fourth byte of every command, one of four 4 096-byte
  payloads rewritten in 16 sectors cut at every eighth, eleven 4 096-byte
  payloads rewritten in turn beside the base's full store, and the
  figures above that the tests pin (2 808 bytes beside the full store in
  3 sectors by the deterministic history, 2 316 before; 4 096 bytes in
  4). C-SEAMS: case region (the test engine linked with `store5.ld` and
  `store16.ld`, both links' regions as set; five regions refused through
  real builds, each saying why and where one would fit), and case
  powercut, whose 4 096-byte rewrite now runs in the 5-sector region and
  which gains a fifth save: in the 16-sector region, one of eleven
  4 096-byte payloads rewritten after 27 rewrites, the ring so full that
  the save moves the head on twice for one part's room, the firmware's
  flash commands the model's one for one, every command in the region,
  cut at every command, the other ten payloads unchanged.
EOF
echo ok

## The wide region test build

store 5 sectors, chip offsets `0xFA000` to `0xFEFFF`: the size a 4 096-byte

the same; `tools/store.py` takes the region's size (`sectors`).

## Versions

Version 1 is the first (M7). The kinds for firmwares built on the base
(clean-1027) are an addition to version 1: their records are version 1's
records, and a reader that doesn't know them skips them. clean-1028's
committed write (the last part) changes no byte of the format, only which
records a reader takes. A later format changes the sector header's
format byte, and says here what changed; a payload's own version changes
when its layout does, and the reader migrates what it knows.

**Where the store goes.** The store's region is yours to choose (R-STORE-12).
By default it is the three sectors at `0xFC000` to `0xFEFFF`, which the
stock layout leaves unused (HW-80); the stock firmware's user patch
region below it (`0xEA000` to `0xFBFFF`) is never touched. To choose
another, set the symbol pair `STORE_BASE` (a chip offset) and
`STORE_SIZE` (bytes) in your linker script, before it includes the
platform's:

```
/* src/my.ld */
STORE_BASE = 0x84000;     /* 16 sectors, 0x84000 to 0x93FFF */
STORE_SIZE = 0x10000;

INCLUDE platform.ld

ASSERT(my_record == 0x01C00870, "my record must follow the store's")
```

The store's code is the same in any region; it reads the pair as link
symbols (`sb_store_base` and `sb_store_size`, which `nm app.elf` shows).
The build checks the region on both links (the raw image and the
package's, whose image is 0x120 bytes longer) and prints it:

```
app-pkg.elf: store region 0x84000 to 0x93FFF, 16 sectors (the image ends at 0x1F8E7)
```

(for an image of about 110 KiB; the lines below are for the same image).

It refuses a region, saying what is wrong and where one of that size
would fit, if it:

- doesn't start on a 4 KiB sector boundary, or isn't whole sectors;
- is smaller than 3 sectors (the store's minimum) or larger than 128
  (`STORE_SECTORS_MAX`, what the store keeps track of);
- overlaps your image (it starts at chip offset `0x4000`), or the boot
  area below it;
- crosses the end of the app area at `0x94000`, or lies past it in the
  stock layout: the VM region (`0x94000` to `0xE8FFF`), the Bluetooth
  sector, the stock user patch region, or the chip's last sector (its
  per-unit key, which must never be erased).

So a region goes either in the app area after your image, or in the
unused three sectors. `0x94000` is where the stock layout's app area
ends (HW-80); the hardware facts give the app area's start but no fixed
end, so this is the conservative reading until SR-11 is answered. For
example:

```
app.elf: store region: the region (0x10000 to 0x14FFF) overlaps the image, which ends at chip offset 0x1F8E7: start it at 0x20000 or later
app.elf: store region: where it would fit: a region of 5 sectors fits in the app area after the image, from 0x20000 to 0x8F000 at the latest; the unused region 0xFC000 to 0xFEFFF holds 3 (the default, STORE_BASE 0xFC000, STORE_SIZE 0x3000)
FAIL: the store's region doesn't fit (above; tools/store-region.pl)
```

How large: saves are atomic, so a rewrite needs room for the old payload
and the new one beside everything else live. The rule: everything live
plus the new payload's records must fit in the region's sectors but one
(the ring keeps one free to move on), each sector holding 4 080 bytes
of records, a part's record (512 bytes for a full one) never split
across two; a 4 096-byte payload is 9 parts, 4 288 bytes as records. In

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Runs every check on a pull request's head commit (the commit the owner
# will merge) and uploads the report as an artifact. Never writes to the
# records branch: records are written only by records.yml, for main.
name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 75
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install check tools
        run: python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check -r tools/requirements-ci.txt

      # C-PERF's baseline: the latest record of a main commit.
      - name: Fetch the records branch
        run: git fetch --no-tags origin +refs/heads/records:refs/remotes/origin/records

      - name: Run all checks
        env:
          COMMIT_RANGE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}..${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PERF_BASE_REF: origin/main
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # The owner's private terms, for C-PRIVATE (tools/check-private.py
          # prints only file and line, never a term).
          PRIVATE_TERMS: ${{ secrets.PRIVATE_TERMS }}
        run: python tools/record.py run --out out/record

      # The performance verdict, improvements included, on the pull
      # request's checks page (R-PERF-2).
      - name: Performance summary
        if: always()
        run: python tools/perf.py summary --record out/record/report.json >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true

      - name: Upload report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: ci-report-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          path: out/record
          if-no-files-found: error

**Third and last in the merge order, after #169 and #170** (cumulative: it holds their commits). One commit of its own (BR-11), three commits completing this session's EXPOSURE entry, and two merges of #170's later commits (its perf probe fix and its fourth power-cut save).

**What:** BR-11, per-folder compiler flags. `tools/build.sh build` now takes `--cflags DIR FLAGS`, `--cxxflags DIR FLAGS` and `--asflags DIR FLAGS`, each repeatable, beside `--src` and `--leave-out`.
- FLAGS go after the firmware's own flags, for the C, C++ or assembly files under DIR. DIR is a `--src` folder or a folder inside one.
- A file under several such folders gets each folder's flags, in the order given, so an inner folder can override an outer one.
- The base's own files, its runtime included, keep the base's flags.
- Relative paths in `-I`, `-isystem` and `-iquote` are taken from DIR.
- **Accepted:** only the flag families firmware code needs: `-D`, `-U`, `-O`, `-W`, `-w`, `-f`, `-m`, `-std=`, `-I`, `-isystem`, `-iquote`, `-g`, `-pedantic`, `-ansi`.
- **Refused:** absolute paths and `..`; the prefix maps, `-fprofile…`, `-fplugin…`, `-fpass-plugin…`, `-fsave-optimization-record`, `-Wa,`, `-Wp,` and `-Wl,`; anything outside the families above; any character but letters, digits and `_ = + . , / : -`. These would reach the host, break determinism or undo the build.
- Documented in BUILDING-ON-SMALL-BEEPS.md, section 5, with an example.

**Why:** the owner's prompt for this session, section 2 (BR-11). Adds R-BUILD-5. docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md has "per-folder compiler flags (BR-11, R-BUILD-5)".

**How:**
- The host checks the flags, maps each folder to its mount in the container (`../sb-src-N/...`), and passes everything as `SB_FOLDER_FLAGS`. `build_outside` then adds each matching folder's flags to the file's compile line.
- New seams case `flags`, using `tests/seams/flags`. Its C, C++ and assembly files each `#error` without their flags. The outer C file also fails if the base's `-Os` came after its `-O2`. A C file in `inner/` needs both folders' flags and its own `-Iinclude`.

**Result:**
- **seams `flags` PASS:**
  - each file's compile line ends with its folders' flags, in order, after the base's, and its symbol is in the ELF;
  - the base's compile lines carry none of the folders' flags, and those of `firmware/src/` match the build without them (which stops on the folder's files);
  - built from two copies of the folder elsewhere on the host, one with the source mounted elsewhere: the same bytes;
  - 11 refusals.
- **The whole seams suite PASS on this branch except `flags`'s first run.** The container looked the options up under another name; that is fixed, and `flags` and `outside` were rerun and pass. The suite took 34 minutes, the `powercut` case included.
- **Build A is unchanged:** `app.bin` is `c5063ae4…`, the same as #170's.
- All 389 unit tests pass.

**Sources:** none
**Exposure:** firmware side, none (claude-opus-5-5)

**Record:** filled in after merge: `records/<merge commit>/` on the `records` branch

         defaults (today's three sectors at 0xFC000), which a firmware's
         own linker script sets before INCLUDE platform.ld; the store
         reads them as link symbols (sb_store_base, sb_store_size), its
         tables sized for STORE_SECTORS_MAX (128). tools/store-region.pl,
         run by tools/build.sh on both links, refuses a region off sector
         boundaries, under 3 or over 128 sectors, over the image or the
         boot area, across the app area's end (0x94000) or in the stock
         layout past it, saying what is wrong and where one would fit.
         make_room moves the ring on while the new head has no room (once
         round at most); STORE_FW_KEYS 32 -> 128. SB_TEST_STORE_WIDE gone:
         the test engine's store5.ld and store16.ld (from 0x20000). Seams
         case region; powercut in 5 and 16 sectors; SR-11 filed.
Why:     the owner's answer (clean-store-region, section 1); R-STORE-12.
         The worked example, 16 sectors for several 4 096-byte records,
         needed the ring and key changes: before them 16 sectors kept 1
         rewritable such payload beside the base's full store.
How:     link symbols, not a define, so one store.o runs in any region; a
         perl check over nm, not ld ASSERTs, whose messages can't carry
         numbers. 0x94000 is HW-80's stock app-area end: the conservative
         reading until SR-11. The room-making loop only goes on where the
         old code refused, so every save that worked makes the same
         commands.

store: each firmware chooses its own store region

What:    firmware/platform.ld sets STORE_BASE and STORE_SIZE with DEFINED()
         defaults (today's three sectors at 0xFC000), which a firmware's
         own linker script sets before INCLUDE platform.ld; the store
         reads them as link symbols (sb_store_base, sb_store_size), its
         tables sized for STORE_SECTORS_MAX (128). tools/store-region.pl,
         run by tools/build.sh on both links, refuses a region off sector
         boundaries, under 3 or over 128 sectors, over the image or the
         boot area, across the app area's end (0x94000) or in the stock
         layout past it, saying what is wrong and where one would fit.
         make_room moves the ring on while the new head has no room (once
         round at most); STORE_FW_KEYS 32 -> 128. SB_TEST_STORE_WIDE gone:
         the test engine's store5.ld and store16.ld (from 0x20000). Seams
         case region; powercut in 5 and 16 sectors; SR-11 filed.
Why:     the owner's answer (clean-store-region, section 1); R-STORE-12.
         The worked example, 16 sectors for several 4 096-byte records,
         needed the ring and key changes: before them 16 sectors kept 1
         rewritable such payload beside the base's full store.
How:     link symbols, not a define, so one store.o runs in any region; a
         perl check over nm, not ld ASSERTs, whose messages can't carry
         numbers. 0x94000 is HW-80's stock app-area end: the conservative
         reading until SR-11. The room-making loop only goes on where the
         old code refused, so every save that worked makes the same
         commands.
Result:  unit tests 402 OK (test_store_region: every refusal; the model in
         5 and 16 sectors); seams region PASS; build A's region 0xFC000,
         3 sectors; 16 sectors keep 11 rewritable 4 096-byte payloads

+By default it is the three sectors at `0xFC000` to `0xFEFFF`, which the
+stock layout leaves unused (HW-80); the stock firmware's user patch

+`STORE_SIZE` (bytes) in your linker script, before it includes the
+platform's:
+/* src/my.ld */
+STORE_BASE = 0x84000;     /* 16 sectors, 0x84000 to 0x93FFF */
+STORE_SIZE = 0x10000;
+INCLUDE platform.ld
+ASSERT(my_record == 0x01C00870, "my record must follow the store's")
+The store's code is the same in any region; it reads the pair as link
+symbols (`sb_store_base` and `sb_store_size`, which `nm app.elf` shows).
+The build checks the region on both links (the raw image and the
+package's, whose image is 0x120 bytes longer) and prints it, here for an

+So a region goes either in the app area after your image, or in the
+unused three sectors. `0x94000` is where the stock layout's app area
+ends (HW-80); the hardware facts give the app area's start but no fixed
+end, so this is the conservative reading until SR-11 is answered. For
+example, 5 sectors from `0x10000` with the same image:
+app.elf: store region: the region (0x10000 to 0x14FFF) overlaps the image, which ends at chip offset 0x1F7C7: start it at 0x20000 or later

+app.elf: store region: where it would fit: a region of 5 sectors fits in the app area after the image, from 0x20000 to 0x8F000 at the latest; the unused region 0xFC000 to 0xFEFFF holds 3 (the default, STORE_BASE 0xFC000, STORE_SIZE 0x3000)
+FAIL: the store's region doesn't fit (above; tools/store-region.pl)
+How large: saves are atomic, so a rewrite needs room for the old payload
+and the new one beside everything else live. The rule: everything live
+plus the new payload's records must fit in the region's sectors but one
+(the ring keeps one free to move on), each sector holding 4 080 bytes
+of records, a part's record (512 bytes for a full one) never split
+across two; a 4 096-byte payload is 9 parts, 4 288 bytes as records. In
+practice, from the store's model (`tools/store.py`) over random
+histories:
+| Region | One payload, alone: the largest | One payload beside the base's full store | 4 096-byte payloads, each rewritable: alone (beside the base's full store) |
+| 3 sectors (the default) | 3 920 bytes | 2 444 bytes | none |
+| 5 sectors | 5 904 (the most a payload takes) | 5 904 | 2 (2) |
+**A worked example: 16 sectors for several 4 096-byte records.** Say your
+firmware keeps eight 4 096-byte records (kinds `0x80`, ids 0 to 7: a
+bank of samples, say) and rewrites any of them at any time. Today's
+three sectors can't rewrite even one. Sixteen sectors (64 KiB) keep
+twelve, each rewritable, so eight leaves room to grow. Put them where
+your image can grow into the space below them: the highest place in the
+app area, `0x84000` to `0x93FFF` (the script above), leaves your image
+room to grow to 512 KiB (`0x4000` to `0x83FFF`); the build will refuse
+it the day the image reaches the store. Everything else is as before:
+for (id = 0; id < 8; id++)
+    n = store_get(0x80, id, rec, sizeof rec, &version);   /* at start-up */
+r = store_put(0x80, id, 1, rec, 4096);                    /* from your serve */
+A larger region costs some time: `store_init` reads every sector, and
+those holding your kinds' records three times, so with eleven 4 096-byte
+payloads in 16 sectors it takes 18 ms (in fwtest; 2.2 ms for one in 5
+sectors, 1.1 ms for today's three holding the base's records and two
+small payloads). Call it once, in your init, before the audio starts.
+And a save in a nearly full region may move the ring on several sectors
+(an erase each, up to 12 ms on the chip, HW-77) before it has room. Three
+things to know about a region in the app area:
+- It is yours from the first start: the store finds it erased (or
+  holding what it holds) and formats sectors as it needs them. Moving the
+  region later starts an empty store; nothing moves your data for you.
+- Your own `.fwsc` package writes nothing past your image (section 6),
+  but whether an update erases the rest of the app area is not yet known
+  (SR-11). Until it is answered, treat a store there as surviving your
+  own builds in fwtest and the app, not yet as surviving an update on a
+  unit.
+- The stock firmware's package covers the whole app area (`0x00000` to
+  `0x93FFF`, HW-80), so returning a unit to the stock firmware erases a
+  store there; the default region survives it.

def check_fmgold(case_dir):
    """Every test patch against the golden WAV (R-FM-8); and fmgold2,
    the same run again, gives the same bytes (R-FM-9)."""
    problems, lines, _, _, _ = check_audio_common(os.path.basename(case_dir), case_dir)
    more, _ = fm_common(os.path.basename(case_dir), case_dir, 8)
    problems += more
    other = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(case_dir), "fmgold")
    if os.path.basename(case_dir) == "fmgold2":
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "audio.wav"), "rb") as f1, open(os.path.join(other, "audio.wav"), "rb") as f2:
            same = f1.read() == f2.read()
        lines.append("  the second run's audio.wav is %s the first's" % ("byte for byte" if same else "NOT"))
        if not same:
            problems.append("fmgold2: the output differs from fmgold's")
    return problems, lines

content.content:
# The timing goldens' policy (since overnight-1025; tools/goldtime.py,
# docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, "Timing goldens"):
# - Every --ms of a case with --ipb ends at least 1 ms before the next
#   audio block's end and 0.2 ms after the last one's (a run that ends
#   while core 0 waits ends late, docs/HARNESS.md "Time"; a bigger image
#   moves the blocks later), so a WAV or an end capture never gains or
#   loses a block by a few microseconds. tools/fw-suite.py checks it from
#   each run's ipb.csv and names the --ms to take instead (in the same
#   block where it can be, which changes no golden).
# - MIDI out's golden captures are in golden-midi/<case>/, not in the
#   --golden folders: tools/fw-suite.py compares them, the same bytes in
#   the same order, each within a block and two bytes (2.091 ms) of its
#   golden time.
# - The screens that show the live spectrum while a sound plays
#   (macros, midipanel, spectrum) are in golden-live/<case>/:
#   tools/fw-suite.py compares them exactly outside the spectrum's
#   rectangle, which shows the sound's last few blocks (the spectrum
#   case checks its bars through the interface's record).
# - A golden that moved with the timing only is written again only by
#   tools/regolden.py --out <the suite's --out> [--write]: it proves each
#   change a pure time shift first (the same MIDI bytes; the same sounds,
#   sample for sample, moved by whole frames; a live screen the same
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Writes timing goldens again, only after proving the change a pure time
shift (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, "Timing goldens"; tools/goldtime.py, rule 3).

  regolden.py --out DIR [--only NAME ...] [--write]
      DIR: tools/fw-suite.py's --out. Every golden file of
      tests/fw/boot.suite's cases (their --golden folders,
      tests/fw/golden-midi/ and tests/fw/golden-live/) against that run's
      output of the same name.
  regolden.py --arp-out NEW --arp-old OLD [--only NAME ...] [--write]
      tests/fw/golden/arp.json's sound hashes: NEW and OLD are
      tools/arp_suite.py's --out on the new image and on the base image
      (whose WAVs must give the golden hashes); a hash moves only if the
      two runs' WAVs are the same sounds, moved.
  regolden.py --presets-out NEW --presets-old OLD [--only P01 ...] [--write]
      The same for tests/fw/golden/presets.json (M8b; tools/preset_suite.py's
      --out on the new image and on the base image).

For each golden file it prints "same", "shift" (proven: the same bytes,
notes and sound, only their times moved, with how far; for a screen in
golden-live/, the same outside the live spectrum, which shows the sound)
or "REFUSED" (and why). --write copies the proven ones over their goldens, and only if
nothing was refused: a change that is not a time shift is a change of
behaviour, made by hand in the commit that changes the behaviour, which
says so. When midiout's capture moves, tools/midi_scripts.py writes
midiround's script from it again.
"""

940      enc 6 +1
1000     key 30 tap 250
1390     enc 6 +1
1450     key 30 tap 250
1550     key 33 tap 100
1840     enc 6 +1
1900     key 30 tap 250
2290     enc 6 +1
2350     key 30 tap 250
2740     enc 6 +1
2800     key 30 tap 250
3190     enc 6 +1
3250     key 30 tap 250
3640     enc 6 +1
3700     key 30 tap 250

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""The timing goldens' policy (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, "Timing goldens"),
for the suites that compare fwtest's outputs with golden files.
A bigger or slower image starts a few microseconds later, and every
event of the firmware's that waits on an audio block can then move by a
block (1.451 ms) or by a MIDI byte (0.320 ms). The rules:
1. A run's end clears the audio blocks: the end asked for (--ms) falls
   at least END_BEFORE_MS before the next block's end and at least
   END_AFTER_MS after the last one. An end comes late, never early, while
   core 0 waits (docs/HARNESS.md, "Time"), and start-up only moves the
   blocks later, so the margins say how far either can go before the run
   takes one block more or less (check_end, from the run's ipb.csv).
2. MIDI out's captures are compared with a stated tolerance: the same
   bytes in the same order (the same messages, decoded), each at its
   golden time within MIDI_TOL_MS: a block and two bytes (compare_midi).
   Screens that show the live spectrum while a sound plays are compared
   exactly outside its rectangle (LIVE), which shows the sound's last
   few blocks and so moves with them; the spectrum case checks the bars
   themselves through the interface's record (compare_screen).
3. Goldens are written again only by tools/regolden.py, which proves the
   change a pure time shift first (the same bytes, notes and sound) and
   writes nothing otherwise (the shift_* functions here).
"""
BLOCK_FRAMES = 64                       # stereo frames a block (firmware/src/audio.h)
BLOCK_MS = BLOCK_FRAMES * 544 / 24000.0  # 1.451 ms (HW-45)
BYTE_MS = 0.32                          # a MIDI byte on the wire
END_BEFORE_MS = 1.0
END_AFTER_MS = 0.2
MIDI_TOL_MS = BLOCK_MS + 2 * BYTE_MS    # 2.091 ms
QUIET = 1                               # |sample| at or under this is quiet: a level held at -96 dB leaves +-1
GAP_FRAMES = 2 * BLOCK_FRAMES           # quiet frames that part two sounds
MAX_SHIFT_FRAMES = 16 * BLOCK_FRAMES    # how far one sound may move (23 ms)
# The live spectrum on the patch view (firmware/src/views.c: SPEC_X,
# SPEC_Y, SPEC_BARS bars 4 pixels apart, SPEC_H): x, y, width, height.
LIVE = [(8, 150, 56 * 4, 40)]
# --- 1. A run's end -------------------------------------------------------
def block_ends(case_dir):
    """The time each audio block ended (ipb.csv's end_ms), or None."""
    path = os.path.join(case_dir, "ipb.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    with open(path) as f:
        rows = [l.strip().split(",") for l in f if l.strip()][1:]
    return [float(r[1]) for r in rows]

**Second and last in the merge order, after #172** (cumulative: it holds #172's commits). Its own commits: the store region, a power-cut test fix, fmgold's script, store.h's figures, and merges of #172's later commits.

**What:** each firmware chooses its own store region (the owner's answer, prompt section 1; R-STORE-12).
- **Default unchanged.** small-beeps keeps three sectors at `0xFC000` to `0xFEFFF`. The stock user patch region (`0xEA000` to `0xFBFFF`) is untouched.
- **A firmware sets its own region** with the symbol pair `STORE_BASE` and `STORE_SIZE` in its linker script, before `INCLUDE platform.ld` (`DEFINED()` defaults in `firmware/platform.ld`).
- **The store reads the region at run time,** as link symbols (`sb_store_base`, `sb_store_size`), so one compiled `store.c` runs in any region of 3 to 128 sectors (`STORE_SECTORS_MAX`). The format is unchanged.
- **`tools/store-region.pl`**, run by `tools/build.sh` on both links (`app.elf` and `app-pkg.elf`), refuses a region that:
  - doesn't start on a sector boundary or isn't whole sectors;
  - is under 3 or over 128 sectors;
  - overlaps the image or the boot area;
  - crosses the app area's end (`0x94000`);
  - lies in the VM region, the Bluetooth sector, the stock user patch region or the last sector.

  Each message says what is wrong and where a region of that size would fit.
- **The app area's end is a reading.** HW-87 to HW-93 give the area's start and its length but no fixed end, so `0x94000` (HW-80's stock layout) is the conservative reading. **SR-11** asks the spec side about it.
- **Two store changes the worked example needed.** Without them, 16 sectors kept only one rewritable 4 096-byte payload beside the base's full store.
  - `make_room` now moves the ring on while the new head has no room, once round at most. It only goes on where the old code refused, so every save that worked before makes the same commands.
  - `STORE_FW_KEYS` goes from 32 to 128 (1.5 KiB of RAM).
- **Test regions.** `SB_TEST_STORE_WIDE` (5 sectors from `0xFA000`, which the check now refuses) is replaced by the test engine's `store5.ld` and `store16.ld`, 5 and 16 sectors from `0x20000`, after its image.
- **Documentation.** BUILDING-ON-SMALL-BEEPS.md has "Where the store goes", with the sizing rule and a worked example: 16 sectors at `0x84000` for several 4 096-byte records. DESIGN-NOTES, STORE-FORMAT and REQUIREMENTS are updated (R-STORE-1, R-STORE-10, R-STORE-11, new R-STORE-12).
- **fmgold's script:** its last note's release moves from 3950.0 to 3950.7 ms; its golden does not change.

**Why:** the owner's prompt for this session, section 1.

**How:**
- Link symbols rather than a define: a firmware's own linker script is the place the owner named, and the base's objects don't change per firmware.
- A perl check over `nm` rather than ld `ASSERT`s: an `ASSERT`'s message can't carry numbers.
- The sizing rule: everything live plus the new payload's records must fit in the region's sectors but one, at 4 080 bytes of records a sector, with no record split across sectors.

**Result** (all from copies of the tree, one suite at a time):

| Suite | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Unit tests | 402 OK, 10 new in `test_store_region` (every refusal) |
| Seams suite | PASS, all ten cases |
| Firmware suite | PASS |
| ARP suite | PASS |
| Package suite | PASS |
| Presets | 70 of 70 |
| perf | PASS, every budget held (no baseline here) |

- **Seams `region`:** the test engine in 5 and 16 sectors. Five regions are refused through real builds, each saying why and where one would fit.
- **Seams `powercut`:** five saves, 724 cuts, never neither and never a mix. The new 16-sector save rewrites one of eleven 4 096-byte payloads after 27 rewrites. It moves the ring twice for one part's room, in 65 commands with 260 cuts, and its flash commands are the model's, one for one.
- **Capacity, from `tools/store.py`'s model over random histories:**

  | Region | One payload beside the base's full store | Rewritable 4 096-byte payloads beside it | Alone |
  |-------:|------:|------:|------:|
  | 3 sectors | 2 444 bytes (was 1 664) | none | none |
  | 4 sectors | 4 284 bytes | 1 (was none) | 1 |
  | 16 sectors | 5 904 bytes | 11 (was 1) | 12 |
- **Start-up** (`store_init`, measured in fwtest):

  | Region and contents | Time |
  |-------|-----:|
  | Default region, the base's records alone (persist case) | 281.2 µs (275.2 µs before) |
  | Default region, the base's full store and two small payloads | 1.13 ms |
  | 5 sectors, one 4 096-byte payload | 2.17 ms |
  | 16 sectors, eleven 4 096-byte payloads | 18.1 ms |
- **Image:** code 55 240 bytes (55 108 before), bss 2 272 bytes more. perf: startup 1 070 916 instructions, steady state 1 886.0 per period, loaded 109 166 per period, stack 572 bytes.
- **fmgold:** the first firmware-suite run failed fmgold and fmgold2. The release at 3950.0 ms fell within 10 µs of a block edge; on both main's image and this one, 249.99 ms gives one output and 250.01 ms the golden. This image's blocks run 0.011 ms later, which tipped it over. 250.7 ms gives the golden on both, with 0.5 ms of margin either side.
- **Powercut:** its first run failed only the new command comparison, which compared the model's byte offsets against the pages fwtest logs. Fixed.

**Sources:** none
**Exposure:** firmware side, none (claude-opus-5-5)

**CI run:** this pull request's `ci` run (its artifact holds the report)
**Record:** filled in after merge: `records/<merge commit>/` on the `records` branch

---
name: ci-artifacts-named-files
description: "Clean side: a CI report artifact downloaded whole carries the record's harness/ folder; take named files only, and how to find and fix a C-SEP-TERMS hit"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cd82f4be-e875-4959-b383-d66813d290ce
  modified: 2026-10-25T17:40:00.000Z
---

A `gh run download` of a CI report artifact brings the whole record, including its `harness/` folder of harness test results. M7 (2026-10-24) did that twice, opened only named logs, deleted both and recorded it in EXPOSURE.md.

**Why:** the clean-room rules let clean sessions take only named files of the firmware's own records; a whole artifact is the record wholesale.

**How to apply:**
- Read CI results from `gh run view <id> --log` first.
- If an artifact file is needed, name the file: ARP (2026-10-25) fetched the zip by API and ran `unzip -p zip logs/C-SEP-TERMS.log` (nothing else extracted), then deleted the zip at once and recorded it.
- C-SEP-TERMS gives only a place and a hash (`sha256(word)[:16]`). Hash the flagged line's words the same way to find the word.
- C-SEP-TERMS also scans commit messages and PR texts: a rename commit, PR text or EXPOSURE entry must never name the flagged word, or it fails again (ARP had to reword and force-push a commit).
- Pick names unlikely to be emulator identifiers (a plain `keys_*` name was one).
- A false positive goes in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json` by its own PR, which keeps a budget PR clean.

Related: [[provenance-ids-race]]

name: ci-artifacts-named-files
description: "Clean side: a CI report artifact downloaded whole carries the record's harness/ folder; take named files only, and how to find and fix a C-SEP-TERMS hit"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cd82f4be-e875-4959-b383-d66813d290ce
  modified: 2026-10-25T17:40:00.000Z
---

A `gh run download` of a CI report artifact brings the whole record, including its `harness/` folder of harness test results. M7 (2026-10-24) did that twice, opened only named logs, deleted both and recorded it in EXPOSURE.md.

**Why:** the clean-room rules let clean sessions take only named files of the firmware's own records; a whole artifact is the record wholesale.

**How to apply:**
- Read CI results from `gh run view <id> --log` first.
- If an artifact file is needed, name the file: ARP (2026-10-25) fetched the zip by API and ran `unzip -p zip logs/C-SEP-TERMS.log` (nothing else extracted), then deleted the zip at once and recorded it.
- C-SEP-TERMS gives only a place and a hash (`sha256(word)[:16]`). Hash the flagged line's words the same way to find the word.
- C-SEP-TERMS also scans commit messages and PR texts: a rename commit, PR text or EXPOSURE entry must never name the flagged word, or it fails again (ARP had to reword and force-push a commit).
- Pick names unlikely to be emulator identifiers (a plain `keys_*` name was one).
- A false positive goes in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json` by its own PR, which keeps a budget PR clean.

Related: [[provenance-ids-race]]

content.text: <total_tokens>14563921 tokens left</total_tokens>

Done, ready to clear.

## Questions

1. **The store did not stay strictly "unchanged".** You said it works unchanged in any region of 3 sectors or more. It does, but your worked example didn't: with the old code, 16 sectors could keep only one rewritable 4 096-byte record beside the base's own records. Two changes fixed that:
   - The store now keeps moving to the next sector until it has room, at most once round. Every save the old code accepted makes exactly the same flash writes as before; only saves it used to refuse behave differently.
   - It now tracks 128 record parts instead of 32 (1.5 KiB of RAM). A 4 096-byte record is 9 parts, so 32 ran out at three such records.

   Is that acceptable?
2. **The build refuses more regions than the five you listed.** It also refuses regions over 128 sectors, in the boot area, in the stock firmware's VM region (its settings, and where an update stages its loader), the Bluetooth sector, and the per-unit last sector. HARDWARE-SPEC says a store must or should stay out of each of these. Should the VM region be allowed?
3. **SR-11 is filed.** HW-87 to HW-93 give where the app area starts, but no fixed end, so the build takes 0x94000 (the stock layout's end) as the conservative reading. The request also asks whether an update erases flash between our image and 0x94000. Until it's answered, the guide says a store there survives fwtest and the app, but not yet an update on a real unit. Returning a unit to the stock firmware erases it; the default region survives that.
4. **The PLAITS_HWFLOAT exception is gone.** The 68 write-back stores the check had counted in that build were all misreadings of a float instruction. With the right disassembly it has none. One narrow new allowance replaces it: the firmware suite's bad-instruction test build, which contains undecodable bytes on purpose.
5. **I changed one line of the fmgold test script, not its golden.** The last key release moved from 3950.0 to 3950.7 ms. At 3950.0 it sat within 10 µs of an audio block edge: on both main's image and the new one, 249.99 ms gave one output and 250.01 ms gave the golden. The new image is slightly bigger, its blocks run 0.011 ms later, and that tipped it over the edge.
6. **A full 16-sector region is slow at start-up: 18.1 ms in fwtest** with eleven 4 096-byte records. For comparison: 2.2 ms for one record in 5 sectors, 1.1 ms for today's region with the base's records and two small payloads. It happens once, in the firmware's init. Is that acceptable, or should I look at speeding it up?

## What was done

- **Setup:** the role file says `clean`. clean-1028's transcript is archived and `check-transcripts.py` passes (23 transcripts). The prompt is saved unedited as `docs/prompts/clean-store-region.md`, and this session's EXPOSURE entry is written. Disk was 6.1 GB free at the start and 4.5 GB at the lowest.
- **#172, BR-13:** the write-back check now disassembles each object with the CPU and float flags it was compiled with, and refuses any instruction it can't read. A float-heavy test object passes. Main's check wrongly refuses it, and the new check finds a real store planted after the float code. CI is green.
- **#173, the store region:**
  - A firmware sets `STORE_BASE` and `STORE_SIZE` in its own linker script; the default stays three sectors at 0xFC000.
  - The build checks both links and, for each bad region, says what's wrong and where one of that size would fit.
  - The guide has a "Where the store goes" section, with the sizing rule and a worked example: 16 sectors from 0x80000 for several 4 096-byte records.
  - DESIGN-NOTES, STORE-FORMAT and the requirements (new R-STORE-12) are updated, and SR-11 is filed.
  - Tests:
    - 402 unit tests pass, including one per refusal.
    - Power cuts run in 5 and 16 sectors: 724 cuts over five saves, never neither copy and never a mix.
    - Seams, firmware, ARP, package and preset suites pass (70 of 70 presets); perf passes every budget.

    CI is green.
  - CI's first run failed the emulator-terms check: two hex numbers (the example's start address and a test value) matched emulator-only terms. I replaced them.
- **One attempt that fetched nothing:** a `git archive main` needed a file this folder leaves out. Lazy fetching is off, so it stopped without downloading anything. It's recorded in EXPOSURE.

## Merge order

1. #172 (`build/disasm-flags`)
2. #173 (`store/region`, which contains #172's commits)
